entries.english:
331. चतुर and अनडुह get the acutely accented augment आ (आम्) after the उ in the strong cases.

Thus अनडुह् + सु = अनडुआह् + सु ॥ Then applies the following rule.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
332. अनडुह् gets the augment नुम् before the ending of the Nom. Sg. (and Vocative).

By the last अनडुह् gets the augment आ or अ after उ in the strong cases, and अ in Vocative Singular (VII. 1. 99) It thus becomes अनड्वाह् and अनड्वह् ॥ By the present sūtra नुम् is added after this आ and अ ॥ The case-ending is elided by VI. 1. 68, and the final ह् by VIII. 2. 23. Thus we have अनड्वान् Nominative Singular ; and अनड्वन् in the Vocative Singular. The augments आम् and अम् (VII. 1. 98, 99), do not supersede नुम्, nor are they superseded by नुम् ॥

The नुम् is specifically taught by this Sūtra, the व् is not changed to द by VIII. 2. 72 S 334. The final is not elided, because the elision of ह् by VIII. 2. 23. S 54 is not perceived by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236, requiring the elision of न because of the rule VIII. 2. 1. S 12. So the न is not elided. Thus the Nom : Sing is अनड्वान्. In forming the Voc : the following rule applies.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
333. चतुर् and अनडुह् get the augment अ after the उ in the Vocative Singular.

This debars the previous rule. As, हे अनड्वन्, हे अनड्वाहौ, अनड्वाहः ॥

The Instr : Sing. is अनडुहा.

Before the affixes भ्याम्, भिः &c, the ह् is changed to द by the following rule.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
334. द is substituted for the final of a word formed with the affix वसु and ending in स् and for the final of स्रंसु, ध्वंसु and अनडुह् at the end of a Pada (in the wider sense I. 4. 14, 17).

Thus अनडुद्भ्याम् &c.

Why do we say that the word formed with the affix वसु must end in स् ? Observe विद्वान्.

Why do we say final in a Pada? Observe स्रस्तम्, ध्वस्तम्.

Now, we take up the declension of तुरासाह्. In its declension, the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Restored initial 'द' and affix 'वसु' in heading.

entries.english:
335. ष is substituted for the स् in साह्, when this occurs in the form of साड् (षाड्) ॥

Thus तुराषाट्. साड् is derived from सह् by the affix ण्वि (III. 2. 63 S 3409), there is vṛiddhi of the penultimate, the ह् is changed to ढ (VIII. 2. 31) and the upapada is lengthened (VI. 3. 137 S. 3539).

Note:—साडः सः would have been enough, for there is no other form साड् except this derived from सह् : why then the word सहेः is used in the sūtra ? There is another form साड् not derived from सह् ॥ Thus सह डेन वर्त्तते = सडः, तस्य अपत्यं = साडिः ॥ He in whose name there is the letter ड is called सड ; as मृड ॥

Why do we say 'in the form of साड्' ? The rule will not apply when the form is साह्, as जलासाहम्, तुरासाहम् । Why do we say सः "for the स्" ? So that the आ of साड् may not be changed to cerebral : the ड् is already cerebral.

Here ends the declension of Masculine nouns ending in ह् ॥

There is no masculine noun ending in य् though on the analogy of the Noun कमल (See 340) we may form तोय् meaning तोयमाचक्षाणः and decline as तोय्, तोयौ, तोयः yet this य् will always be elided by the rule VI. 1. 66 S. 373. We take up therefore, the declension of the Masculine nouns ending in व् e.g. सुदिव्.

In its declension, the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Restored ह् and ढ in explanation of VIII. 2. 31.

entries.english:
336. औत् is substituted for the final of the prātipadika दिव् before सु (Nom. sg. and Voc. Sg.)

Note:—There is a nominal stem दिव् which is taken here. It has no indicatory letters annexed to it. The root दिव् is not to be taken here, as it has the in
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Entry text cut off at bottom of page 199; SK number misprinted as ३३४ in Devanagari line; restored औत् at start of heading.

entries.english:
...dicatory letter and is exhibited in the Dhâtupâtha as दिवुँ. The nominal-stem derived from दिव् does not take it, but ‹?›, the Nom. Sg. of which is ‹?› (See VI. 4. 19, and VI. 1. 131).
The rule VI. 1. 68 S. 252, required the elision of ‹?›; but this is prevented, because it is not ‹?› for the purposes of rule VI. 1. 68. S. 252. Thus the Nom: forms are द्यौः, सुद्यौः, अतिद्यौः. The Acc: forms are सुदिवम्, सुदिवौ &c.
Before भ्याम् and भिः the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: Chapter XI
entries.note: Entry begins on previous page; tail continuation on page 200.

entries.english:
337. For the final of the nominal-stem दिव्, there is the substitution of उ, when it is a Pada (I. 4. 14 &c).
Note:—The portion of the word अङ्गस्य must be read into this sûtra from VI. 1. 109. The word दिव् is here a nominal-stem and not a verbal-root. Thus ‹?›. We have said that दिव् is here a prâtipadika and not a dhâtu, for as a dhâtu it ought to have its servile letter (anubandha) and should have been read as दिवुँ. In the case of its being used as a verb, there takes place the substitution of long ऊ by VI. 4. 19. In that case we shall have अक्षद्यूभ्याम्, अक्षद्यूभिः ॥ The उत् with a त् shows that short उ is meant, and debars (VI. 4. 19). In the case of substitution the forms will be सुद्युभ्याम्, सुद्युभिः ॥ The षत्व also comes because it is taught in a subsequent sûtra. Why do we say 'when it is a Pada'? Observe सुदिवौ, सुदिवः ॥
Thus Instr: Dual and Pl. are सुद्युभ्याम्, सुद्युभिः.
Here ends the declension of Masculine nouns ending in व्.
—:o:—
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in र्.
We take up the declension of चतुर् which is always Plural. Its Nom: Pl. is चतुर् + जस् = चतुर् + आम् + अस् (S. 331) = चत्वारः । Its Acc:, Instr:, Dat. and Abl: Pl: are चतुरः, चतुर्भिः, चतुर्भ्यः, चतुर्भ्यः respectively.
In forming the Gen: Pl: the following rule applies:—
entries.chapter: Chapter XI

entries.english:
338. The augment नुट् is added before the Genitive pl. ending आम् after the Numerals called 'shash', and after चतुर् ॥
Text:—The न् is changed to ण् by VIII. 4. 1. S. 235 and this is optionally doubled by VIII. 4. 46. S. 59.
As चतुर्णाम् ॥ A numeral ending in ष् is not 'shash', hence the specific mention of चतुर् ॥
Note:—This rule applies to compounds ending with these numerals, when these latter are the principal member, as परमषण्णाम्, परमपञ्चानाम्, परमचतुर्णाम्, but प्रियपञ्चाम्, प्रियचतुराम्, where the Numerals are secondary (upasarjana).
In forming the Loc. Pl. the following is held in abeyance, because the विसर्जनीय taught there applies to that which is derived from रु and not to every र्.
entries.chapter: Chapter XI

entries.english:
339. Visarjaniya is substituted for the र् called रु (and not any other र्), before the Locative Plural case-affix सु ॥
This rule not applying, we have चतुर् + सु = चतुर् + षु by VIII. 3. 59. S. 212.
Then rule VIII. 4. 46 S. 59 requires optional doubling, but this is set-aside by the following.
entries.chapter: Chapter XI

entries.english:
340. There are not two in the room of a sibilant (शर्), when a vowel follows.
Note:—The word न is to be read into the sûtra. This debars the application of rule VIII. 4. 46, S. 59. Thus कर्षति, वर्षति, प्राकर्षः, अक्षदर्शः ॥
Why do we say अचि 'when a vowel follows'? Observe वृत्ते ॥
Text:—Thus चतुर्षु.
Now, we take up the declension of प्रियचतुर् which may be declined in all numbers (See Note under S. 338). प्रियचतुर् + सु = प्रियचतु + आ + र् + स् (VII. 1. 98. S. 331) = प्रियचत्वाः. In the Voc: Sing. instead of अम् there will be अन् by VII. 1. 99. S. 333. Thus हे प्रियचत्वः । The Nom: Dual and Pl: are प्रियचत्वारौ, प्रियचत्वारः. As चतुर् here is a secondary member of a Compound the augment नुट् required by VII. 1. 55. S. 338 is not added in the formation of the Gen: Pl; Thus we have प्रियचतुराम्. But if the compound be not a Bahuvrihi, and चतुर् be a principal member, then the Genitive Pl. will be परमचतुर्णाम् ॥
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in र्.
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ल्.
Now we take up the declension of कमल. This is derived from the Noun कमलम् or कमला by passing through the चुरादिगण under the rule तत्करोति तदाचष्टे, that is, when the sense is कमलं कमलां वाऽऽचक्षाणः that one speaks of Kamala or Kamalâ. Thus कमल + णिच् (of चुरादिगण). To this we add the affix क्विप् when the णिच् is elided by VI. 4. 51. S. 2313. Thus we get कमल. Its declension is Nom. कमल, कमलौ, कमलाः. Its Loc. Pl. कमलत्सु. (The त् being changed to ल्).
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ल्.
There is no noun ending in ‹?›. Therefore we take up the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in म्. In the declension of these nouns, the following rule applies.
entries.chapter: Chapter XI

entries.english:
341. न् is substituted, at the end of a Pada, for the final म् of a root.
As प्रशान्, this is formed by adding क्विप् to the root शम् ॥ The lengthening takes place by VI. 4. 15. S. 2556. The नत्व being considered as asiddha is not elided by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236.
The word पदस्य is understood here also. So we have प्रशामौ, प्रशामः where म् is not at the end of a pada.
The Nom: forms are प्रशान्, प्रशामौ, प्रशामः ; The Instr: Dual is प्रशान्भ्याम्, &c.
—:o:—
Now, we take up the declension of किम् सर्ववत् ॥ In its declension, the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: Chapter XI
entries.note: Devanagari digit in Panini reference printed/read as 6 instead of 8.

entries.english:
342. क is substituted for किम् before a vibhakti affix.
As कः, कौ, के, कम्, कौ, कान् ॥
The substitution takes place even when the augment अकच् is added. Therefore, the substitute is here क and not अ which latter would have been sufficient for किम्. For कि being replaced by अ (VII. 2. 102), the म् would be left, which would be replaced
entries.chapter: Chapter XI
entries.note: Entry incomplete; continues on next page.

entries.english:
by or had the sûtra been किमोऽत् and the forms would have been the same (क् + अ + अ = क VI. 1. 97) See V. 3. 1, 13 &c. The rest of the declension is similar to that of सर्व ॥

Now, we take up the declension of इदम् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 342 from p. 202; running header page number 195 was mixed into lines in OCR.

entries.english:
343. म् is substituted for the final म् of इदम् in the Nominative Singular.

The substitution of म् for म् is to prevent the अ substitution of VII. 2. 102.

At this stage applies the next sûtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्
entries.note: Restored embedded Devanagari म् and अ from context.

entries.english:
344. अय् is substituted for the इद् of इदम् in the Nom. Sing. masculine.

As अयम् ॥

The case ending is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. In other cases, sûtra VII. 2. 102. S. 265. would apply and there will be Para-rûpa (VI. 1. 97. S. 191) and so will assume the form इद ॥

At this stage, will apply the following rule.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्

entries.english:
345. And म is substituted for the द् of इदम् before a case-affix.

As इमौ, इमे, इमम्, इमौ, इमान् ॥ Thus इदम् + अम् = इद + अम् (VII. 2. 102 S. 265.) = इम + अम् (VII. 2. 109 S. 345) = इमम् (VI. 1. 97, S. 191).

It is a general rule that there is no Vocative case of त्यदादि words.

In forming the Instrumental and other cases, the following rule applies.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्

entries.english:
346. अन is substituted for the इद् of इदम् in the Instrumental singular and the cases that follow, provided that the augment akach is not added.

As अनेन, अनयोः ॥ Why do we say "not when क is added by V. 3. 71"? Observe इमकेन, इमकयोः ॥ The word आप् (आपि) in the sûtra is a pratyâhâra, formed with the आ of टा (Ins. Sg.), and प् of सुप् (Loc. Pl.).

Before consonantal affixes, the following rule applies.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्

entries.english:
347. The इद् of इदम् is elided before an âp case affix beginning with a consonant, provided that the augment अकच् is not added.

Here applies the maxim—"The rule I. 1. 52. S. 42, by which a substitute should take the place of only the final letter of that which is exhibited in the genitive case, is not valid where what is exhibited in the genitive is meaningless, provided the rule teaching the substitution does not teach a change in a reduplicative syllable."

Having elided इद् of इदम्, the only portion that remains now is म् which is replaced by अ VII. 2. 102 S. 265. Thus we have only अ left. Thus अ + भ्याम् ॥ Now VII. 3. 102 S. 202 declares that a final अ is lengthened before a case affix beginning with यञ् ॥ But the solitary अ is initial and cannot therefore be final and so it should not be lengthened. To remove this doubt, we have the following Sûtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्
entries.note: Restored embedded Devanagari (इद्, अ, यञ्) based on grammatical context.

entries.english:
348. An operation should be performed on a single letter, as upon an initial or upon a final.

Thus अ + भ्याम् = आभ्याम् ॥

In forming the Instr : Pl : the following rule applies
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्

entries.english:
349. This substitution of ऐस् (required by VII. 1. 9 S. 203) does not take place after इदम् and अदस्, except when they end in क ॥

Thus अ + भिः = एभिः (VII. 3. 103 S. 205). The dative forms are thus formed:—अ + ङे = अस्मै (VII. 1. 14 S. 215); अ + भ्याम् = आभ्याम्; अ + भ्यः = एभ्यः ॥ The Abl:, Gen: and Loc: forms are as follow:—अस्मात्, (VII. 1. 15 S. 216); आभ्याम्, एभ्यः; अस्य (VII. 1. 12. S. 201); अनयोः (VII. 3. 104 S. 207 and VII. 2. 112. S. 346); एषाम् (VII. 1. 52. S. 217); अस्मिन् (VII. 1. 15. S. 216); एषु (VIII. 3. 59 S. 212).

When अकच् is added the forms are as follows:—Nom: अयकम्, इमको, इमके; Acc: इमकम्, इमको, इमकान्; Instr: इमकेन, इमकाभ्याम्, इमकेः ॥

By the following rule, when इदम् is used in the second clause of a sentence referring to a man already mentioned in the first clause, the form is different in the Instr: and other cases.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्

entries.english:
350. In the room of idam 'this,' in case of its re-employment in a subsequent member of the same sentence and referring to the same thing (anvâdeśa) there is the substitution of अश् which is anudâtta i. e., gravely accented, when the third case-affix and the rest follow.

Note:—The word अन्वादेश means literally saying (âdeśa) 'after' (anu) or after-say or re-employment.

अश् (actually अ) replaces इदम् in all cases except the nominative and the accusative, when anvâdeśa or repetition is implied. अ replaces the whole of इदम् by I. 1. 55 S. 45. and not only the final.

Text:—The substitute अश् will replace इदम्, even when the latter takes the affix अकच् (V. 3. 71.)
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्
entries.note: Corrected OCR errors in embedded Devanagari (अश्, अ, अकच्) in Note and Text.

entries.english:
351. When an affix of the second case or टा (Ins. Sing.) or ओस् (Loc. dual) follows, एन which is anudâtta is the substitute of इदम् and एतद् in the case of its re-employment.

Anvâdeśa means the employment again of what has been employed to direct some operation, to direct another operation. Thus, "The grammar has been studied by him (anena), now set him (enam)
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN म्

entries.english:
to read the Vedas.” or again "of these two (anayoh) the family is illustrious and their (enayah) wealth is great," The cases in this form are:—Acc. एनम्, एनौ, एनान्; Instr: Sing: एनेन; Gen: & Loc. Dual एनयोः ।
Here ends the declension of Masc : Nouns ending in म्.
—:0:—
There is no Masculine noun ending in ङ. Now we take up the declension of Masculine nouns ending in ण् e.g. सुगण् which is formed by the affix विच् added to गण् ( III. 2. 75 S. 2980) Its Nom forms are सुगण्, सुगणौ, सुगणः ; Loc. Pl. is ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›.
If it be formed with the affix क्विप् ( III. 2. 76 S. 2983), then by VI. 4. 15 S. 2666, there is lengthening. Thus the forms will be सुगाण्, सुगाणौ, सुगाणः ; the Loc: Pl: is ‹?›, ‹?›, or ‹?› ।
Here ends the declension of Masc: Nouns ending in ण्.
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in न्.
Now, we take up the declension of राजन्. Its Nom: Sg. is राजन् + सु = राजान् + सु (The penultimate being lengthened by VI. 4. 8 S. 250 ) — राजान् + 0 (the affix being elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252 ) — राजा ( the न् being elided by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236.),
In forming the Voc : the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI
entries.note: Entry is a tail continuation from page 205; SK number 351 inferred from following entry 352.

entries.english:
352. (But such न्) is not elided in the Locative and Vocative Singular.
This debars the elision of न्, which otherwise would have taken place by the sûtra VIII. 2. 7. S. 236. The examples of non-elision of न्, in the Locative singular are to be found in the Vedas. As परमे व्योमन् (Rig. I. 164. 39). Here the sign of the Locative, namely, (ङि) is elided by VII. 1. 39 S. 3561. In the Vocative singular the न् is not elided; as हे राजन्, हे तक्षन् ॥
The very fact of the prohibition of the elision of न्, as contained in this aphorism, indicates by implication (jñâpaka), that a word does get the designation of pada, though an affix has been elided after it by using लुक्, yet such elided affix does sometimes produce its effect in spite of I. 1. 63. S. 263.
Vart:— Prohibition of the prohibition must be stated, when the Locative word is followed by another word in a compound. That is, when a compound is a Locative Tatpurusha, the न् is elided: as, चर्माणि तिला अस्य = चर्मतिलः, ब्रह्मणि निष्ठा अस्य = ब्रह्मनिष्ठः ॥
The Nom : Dual and Pl : are राजानौ ; राजानः ।
The Acc. Sing and Dual are राजानम् ; राजानौ ।
The Acc: Pl. is thus formed:—राजन् + शस् । Here राजन् gets the designation of bha by I. 4. 18. S. 231. and therefore the अ of राजन् is elided by VI. 4. 134 S. 234. and the न् is changed to ञ् by VIII. 4. 40. S. 111. The elision of अ is not Sthanivat, because it is so prohibited in Sûtra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12.
Nor can the elision be considered asiddha on account of its being bahiranga.
There are two aspects under which संज्ञा or technical terms, and Paribhâshâs may be viewed in Panini's Grammar. One is यथोद्देशपक्ष and the other is कार्यकालपक्ष. The former i e यथोद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् means that "Samjnas and Paribhashas remain where they are taught ;" and the latter, i. e. कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् means that "Samjnâs and Paribhashâs are attracted by, or unite with, the rules that enjoin certain operations, provided that Samjnâs occur or are valid in those rules, and provided the Paribhashâs concern them."
Here we take the first alternative and the change of न् into ञ् being asiddha in the view of the rule I. 1. 94. S. 38., there is no antaranga-hood and so the Paribhasha which declares that "antaranga is stronger than bahiranga" finds no scope for application. Therefore ज् and ञ् combining form ज्ञ. Thus we get the Acc. Pl. राज्ञः; Inst. Sing is राज्ञा ॥
Similarly परमे व्योमन् || Here व्योमन् is in the Locative case. व्योमन् + ङि = व्योमन् + 0 (VII. 1. 39, S. 3561) Here the affix is elided by using the word लुक्, and therefore there will be no pratyaya-lakshana (I. 1. 63 S. 263). The result would be that the word व्योमन् would not get the designation of पद (सुप्तिङन्तं पदं) because it has no सुप् after it, so the rule (VIII. 2. 7. S. 236) will not hold good, and therefore there will be no elision of न् of व्योमन्. But in that case the present Sûtra would have been useless. But the very fact that this sûtra is made, indicates that the rule न लुमता is not nitya, and so, there will be pratyayalakshana. That being the case, the word becomes पद, and so rule VIII. 2. 7 would have applied to it, but for this Sûtra.
Although ‹?› excludes and debars ‹?›, but in this case it has been superseded by the former.
Now we take up the formation of Acc. pl.
Thus राजन् + शस् = राज् + 0 + न् + शस् (अल्लोपोऽनः) Here the zero will be sthânivat (by अचः परस्मिन् I. 1. 57 S. 50) That being the case, न् will not be changed to ञ् and so we could not get the form राज्ञः ॥ But the lopâdeśa is not sthânivat, because of the vârttika पूर्वत्रासिद्धे न स्थानिवत् (See Mahâbhâshya I. 1. 58 and Siddhânta VIII. 4. 1)
If it be said that the lopa rule is Bahiranga, because it takes place on account of the affix which is outside; and the change of न् into ञ् is inside it, or antaranga; and therefore the lopa will be asiddha with regard to ञ्, then we reply that there is no relation of Antaranga and Bahiranga here. The Paribhâshâ &c. is derived from the Jñâpaka of वाह ऊठ् (VI. 4. 132 S. 329) which belongs to the VIth Adhyâya and consequently does not see the vidhi of the VIIIth Adhyâya (VIII. 4. 41 S. 111.) by the sûtra पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् and so there will be no antaranga Bhâva. This proceeds on the view of यथोद्देश Paksha.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्

entries.english:
353. The elision of a final न् ( VIII. 2. 7 ) is considered as if not to have taken effect, in applying the following rules; (1) rules regarding case-endings, ( 2 ) rules regarding accents, (3) rules regarding any technical term of Grammar, and (4) rules regarding the augment before a Krit-affix.
The word विधि in the sûtra applies to all the four words preceding it : as सुब्विधि, स्वरविधि &c. The force of the Genitive compound in स्वरविधौ, संज्ञाविधौ, is that of ordaining the existence of something: e. g. when an accent is to be given to a word, or a particular designation is to be given to it or when त् is to be added to it, ( भावसाधन ) ॥ The compound सुब्विधि means however, the rule relating to the case-endings themselves, as well as, the rule which would apply to a word, when a case-ending follows (‹?› ) ॥
( 1 ) सुब्विधिः — As राजभिः, तक्षभिः || Here the elision of न् of राजन् and तक्षन् being asiddha, the भिस् is not changed to ऐस् by VII. 1. 9. S. 203. So also राजभ्याम्, तक्षभ्याम्, राजसु, तक्षसु ॥ Here the finals of राज and तक्ष are not lengthened before सुप् by (VII. 3. 102 S. 202.) nor changed to ए before सुप् by (VII. 3. 103 S. 205 ) : as in नराभ्याम् and नरेषु of the stem ending in अ ॥
The elision of न् taught by VIII. 2. 7 S. 236. would be asiddha by the general rule VIII. 2. 1 S. 12. the specification of the four cases in which it is asiddha shows that it is a restrictive or niyama rule. That is, the elision of न् is considered asiddha only with regard to these four rules, and no other. It is not asiddha in राजीयते ( राजन् + क्यच् + ते = राज + य् + ते = राजीयते III. 1. 8. S. 2657 VII.

entries.english:
4. 33 S. 2658). There would not have been long ई had the नलोप been asiddha. So also in राजायते there is lengthening, ( VII. 4. 25 S. 2298 ) and in राजाश्व there is ekādeśa (VI. 1. 101 S. 85).
On the other hand, from the elision's not being regarded as having taken effect, there is neither prolongation of the vowel (VII. 3. 102 S. 202) nor the change of अ to ए ( VII. 3. 103 S. 205) nor the substitution of ऐस् for भिस (VII. 1. 9. S. 203 ).
Thus Instr : dual and Pl : are राजभ्याम् and राजभिः respectively. The Dative forms are राज्ञे, राजभ्याम्, राजभ्यः ; Abl : and Gen Sing : राज्ञः ; Gen dual and Pl : राज्ञोः and राज्ञाम् respectively. Loc : Sg. राज्ञि or राजनि ॥

Now we take up the declension of प्रतिदिवन् ॥ This word is formed by the Uṇādi affix कनिन् ( Uṇādi I. 156) added to the root प्रतिदिव 'to shine'. It is declined as follows :—Nom: forms are प्रतिदिवा, प्रतिदिवानौ, प्रतिदिवानः ॥
In the Acc: Pl:. the base being bha, the अ of दिवन् is elided (VI. 4. 134. S. 234 ) and then the following rule comes into operation,

entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 353 from preceding page.

entries.english:
354. Of a root ending in र् or व्, the penultimate इ or उ is lengthened, before a consonantal beginning affix.
The lengthening takes place here, the elision of ‹?› is not considered here as sthānivat because of the prohibition in I. 1. 58 S. 57 with regard to दीर्घविधिः and so व् becomes penultimate.
Nor is this elision by VI. 4. 134. S. 234. a bahiraṅga and therefore asiddha, for the purposes of this rule which is an antaraṅga, for the reasons already given above under VIII. 2. 8. S. 352.
Thus Acc : Pl : is प्रतिदीव्यः ॥
Instr: Sg. प्रतिदीव्या &c.
-:0:-
Now we take up the declension of यज्वन् ॥ Its Nom: forms are यज्वा, यज्वानौ, यज्वानः ॥
But in Bha cases there will not be the elision of अ of मन् because of the following prohibition.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्
entries.note: Devanagari examples and characters restored from context.

entries.english:
355. The अ in अन् is not elided when the Bha stem ends in a consonant preceding व् or मन् ॥
Thus Acc : Pl : यज्वनः ॥ Instr: Sing and dual यज्वना, यज्वभ्याम् &c. Similar is the declension of ब्रह्मन् ॥ Nom. ब्रह्मा, ब्रह्माणौ, ब्रह्माणः, Acc. ब्रह्माणम्, ब्रह्माणौ, ब्रह्मणः; Ins. ब्रह्मणा, ब्रह्मभ्याम्, ब्रह्मभिः ॥

Now, we take up the declension of वृत्रहन् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्

entries.english:
356. The penultimate vowel is lengthened only before the affix शि ( Nominative and Accusative Pl. ), when the stem ends in इन्, or हन्, or पूषन् or अर्यमन् and nowhere else.
To this prohibition is the exception contained in the following sūtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्
entries.note: Corrupted Devanagari इन् restored in translation.

entries.english:
357. The penultimate vowels of a stem ending in इन्, हन्, पूषन् or अर्यमन् are lengthened before the affix सु of the Nominative Singular, but not in Vocative Singular.
Thus वृत्रहा ॥ The न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236, and the case-affix by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. In the Vocative singular we have हे वृत्रहन् ॥
The न is changed to ण by VIII. 4. 12 S. 307. Thus we get the following forms N. D. वृत्रहणौ ; N. Pl : वृत्रहणः, Acc: Sg and Dual : वृत्रहणम् and वृत्रहणौ respectively.
In Acc : Pl : the अ of हन् is elided by VI. 4. 134 S. 234 and the ह् is changed to guttural by the following Sūtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्
entries.note: Missing Devanagari characters restored from explicit context.

entries.english:
358. A guttural is substituted for the ह् in हन् before an affix having an indicatory ञ्, or ण् and before न् ॥
The next Sūtra हन्तेरत्पूर्वस्य is divided by the author into two parts, viz., first, हन्तेः and then अत्पूर्वस्य ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्

entries.english:
359. The न, in the root हन्, is changed to ण, when the verb is preceded by a preposition competent to cause the change.
As प्रहण्यात् ॥ This requires the न् of वृत्रहन् to be changed to ण । But to this the second half of the above Sūtra makes an exception,
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्
entries.note: Heading number corrected from misprint 356 to 359; missing character ण restored.

entries.english:
359 A. The न् of हन् is changed to ण when it is preceded by short अ and in no other case, that is to say, when हन् retains the form हन् and not when the अ is elided and हन् assumes the form of घ्न or when the अ is lengthened.
Thus प्रघ्नन्ति ॥ This interpretation is given because it is possible to divide this Sūtra into two by the maxim योगविभागादिष्टसिद्धिः i.e. 'from a rule which we have obtained by taking part of a rule as a separate rule, we are allowed to derive only such results as may be desirable.'
Paribhāṣā :—'A rule, may it enjoin or forbid anything, either enjoins or forbids only that which is nearest to it in some other rule.'
This maxim being set aside by the fact of the योगविभाग the Sūtra VIII. 4. 12 S. 307. ordaining णत्व also ceases. The elision of अ is not sthānivat because otherwise the ह् will never be followed by न and so there will be no scope for Sūtra VII. 3. 54. S. 358. Thus Acc. Pl. is वृत्रघ्नः, Instr. Sing : वृत्रघ्ना &c.
But the optional form वृत्रघ्णः with a cerebral ण instead of dental न, according to the opinion of Mādhava is a mistake, because it is opposed to Kātyāyana and Patañjali. The न is never changed to ण.
The nouns शार्ङ्गिन्, यशस्विन्, अर्यमन्, पूषन् are similarly declined.
यशस्विन् is formed with the affix विन् and not इन्. The इन् portion in यशस्विन् has no meaning ; and so the rules VI. 4. 12. S. 356 and VI. 4. 13. S. 357. should not apply to it. However these rules are applied, in accordance with the following Paribhāṣā,
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN न्
entries.note: Entry 359 A (yogavibhāga of 359); text cuts off at page end.

entries.english:
Paribhasha:—"Whenever अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are taught in Grammar denote by I. 1. 72, something that ends with these, there they represent these combination of letters both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of a meaning".
Loc : Sing of अर्यमन् is ‹?› or ‹?› ॥
Loc. Sing of पूषन् is ‹?› or ‹?› ॥

Now, we take up the declension of मघवन्. In its declension, the following rule applies.
मघवन् ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINES NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Tail fragment of entry SK 359 continuing from preceding page, including transitional prose introducing SK 360.

entries.english:
360. तृ is diversely substituted for the final of मघवन्.
ऋ of तृ is इत्. And thus we get मघवत्.
Here applies the next Sūtra, showing the force of this indicatory,
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINES NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Reconstructed missing stem 'मघवन्' after 'final of' from clear context.

entries.english:
361. Whatever has an indicatory उ, ऋ and ऌ, (with the exception of a root), and the stem अञ्च्, (मञ्चति) get the augment नुम् in the strong cases.

Thus Nom : Sing. is मघवान्. The penultimate अ is lengthened by VI. 4. 14. S. 425. The affix is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. and the त् is elided by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54.

The form being मघवन्त, the elision of त् takes place by the Tripadi rule संयोगान्तस्य लोपः VIII. 2. 23. S. 54. and therefore this elision is not perceived by the दीर्घ rule of the Sixth Book of Panini (i.e. VI. 4. 14. S. 425). The a of वन्त् therefore not being penultimate will not be lengthened, as it is not lengthened in Verbal Nouns like ‹?› &c, where also the elision of त् is held to be asiddha. Why do we lengthen it in the case of मघवन् ? Because of the word बहुलं in the last Sutra VI. 4. 128 S. 360.

As this word मघवान् requires the help of बहुल to give us the proper form, the author of Mahābhashya has effected the formation of मघवान् by the Unadi I. 159, and he has also assumed that the affix मतुप् will effect the same form when added to मघ in secular literature, and therefore he has in his commentary stated that the Sūtra मघवा बहुलं is a redundancy. The author of Bhatti Kavya also uses the form in secular literature as:—

‹?›

"That Maghavan eats fearlessly the sacrificial offerings in the sacrifices."

The Nom : Dual and Pl. will be मघवन्तौ, मघवन्तः ॥

The Voc : Sing will be हे मघवन् ॥

The Acc. forms are मघवन्तम्, मघवन्तौ, मघवतः ॥

Instr: forms are मघवता, मघवद्भ्याम् &c.

When तृ is not substituted for the final न् of मघवन्, then the Nom : Sing is मघवा ॥

Vartika:—In the Chhandas, the affixes इनि and वनिप् are added to nouns in the sense of मतुप् (See Sūtra V. 2. 122. S. 3498). Therefore if the word मघवन् be formed with वनिप् added to मघ then the word मघवन् will have acute accent on the middle in the Chhandas alone, but in the secular literature it has acute accent on the final also. This is the difference, as मघवन्.

The Nom : Dual and Pl. are मघवानौ, मघवानः ॥

In the Sarvanāmasthāna affixes, मघवन्, without तृ is declined like राजन्. Thus N. D. मघवानौ, N. Pl. मघवानः; Acc. S. D. are मघवानम् and मघवानौ.

In forming the Acc. Pl, the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINES NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Reconstructed OCR-corrupted embedded grammatical markers ('त्', 'तृ', 'इनि') from unambiguous grammatical context.

entries.english:
362. The व of श्वन्, युवन् and मघवन् when ending in अन् becomes vocalised, but not before a Taddhita affix.

Thus मघवन् + शस् = मघ् उ अन् + शस् = मघ् उन् + शस् (अ and उ become उ by VI. 1. 108. S. 330) = मघोन + शस् (अ and उ become ओ by VI. 1. 87. S. 69) = मघोनः ॥

Why do we say 'when ending in अन्'? Observe Acc : Pl : मघवतः when the noun is मघवत् and not मघवन् ॥ In this case the Instr : Sg. is मघवता ॥

The feminine form of मघवत् is मघवती । Why do we say 'not before a Taddhita affix'? Observe माघवनम् ॥

The Instr : Sg. and Dual of मघवन् are मघोना, मघवद्भ्याम् &c. Similar is the declension of श्वन् ॥ Thus शुनः (Acc. Pl.), शुना (Instr : S.), श्वभ्याम् (Instr : Dual) &c.

Now we take up the declension of युवन् ॥

युवन् + शस् = यु + उ + न् + शस् ॥

Here the य of युवन् would also require to be vocalised. But this is prevented by the following Sūtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINES NOUNS ENDING IN

entries.english:
363. When a semivowel has been once vocalised, there is no vocalisation of the other semivowel that may precede it in the same word.

So य of युवन् is not vocalised. Therefore, by the inference to be drawn from this rule, the final semivowel is vocalised.

Thus Acc : Pl is यूनः ; Instr : Sg and Dual are यूना, युवभ्याम् and so on.

Note:—Though the rule of vocalisation does not specify what particular semivowel is to be vocalised, yet according to the maxim that the operation is to be performed on the letter nearest to the operator, the second semivowel in the above cases is vocalised and the first is not, by force of this rule. Had the first semi-vowel been vocalised, then there would be no scope for this sutra, because then no semi-vowel will be found preceding a vocalised letter. This sūtra is a jñāpaka that the vocalisation commences with the second of the conjunct semi-vowels.

Though the anuvṛitti of न was understood here, the repetition of this word shows that the prohibition of double vocalisation in the same word applies even when the semivowels are not contiguous. Thus by VI. 1. 133 there is vocalisation of the word युवन्, the व being changed to उ, the य is not changed as इ. It might be objected that when उ of यु, and the samprasāraṇa of व coalesce into one by sandhi rules, then there being the substitution of one long ऊ for the two उ's and this is sthānivat to the original, the य and उ of युवन् should be considered in fact as contiguous and not separated by an intervening letter, and therefore, the explanation given above does not hold good; we reply. The substitution of one long vowel for two vowels, is not considered sthānivat (See I. 1. 58 S. 51). Even though it be considered as sthānivat, it is still a separating letter.

Now, we take up the declension of अर्वन् ॥ Its N. S. is अर्वा, Its Voc : S is हे अर्वन्
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINES NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Reconstructed heavily corrupted Devanagari letters (य, युवन्, न, उ, इ, ऊ, अर्वन्, अर्वा) in the Note and transition paragraph from clear grammatical context.

entries.english: In forming the N. D. and other cases the following rule applies.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN

entries.english:
364. तृ (which is changed to न्त in the strong cases, and forms the feminine in ई unaccented) is substituted for the final of the stem अर्वन्, except in the Nominative singular or when the word is joined with the Negative particle.
The real substitute is तृ, the ॠ is for the sake of making this affix an ऋित्, so that in sarvanāmasthāna cases we have नुम् augment VII. 1. 70, S. 361. Thus अर्वन्तौ, अर्वन्तः, अर्वन्तम्, अर्वन्तौ, अर्वतः, अर्वता, अर्वद्भ्याम्, &c.
Why do we say when not having the negative particle न ? Observe अनर्वा (N. S.). The rest of its declension is similar to that of यज्वन् ॥
In the declension of पथिन्, मथिन् &c. the following rules apply:—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Restored OCR-garbled Devanagari forms (तृ, अर्वन्, अनर्वा, etc.) from clear grammatical context.

entries.english:
365. आत् ( आ ) is substituted for the final of 'pathin', 'mathin' and 'ṛbhukshin', before the ending सु (of the Nom. Sg.).
Though the sthānin here is a nasal (i. e. न्), yet the substitute आ is not to be nasalised by the rule of nearness (I. 1. 50. 39) but to be pronounced purely, for the आत् of the sûtra is really आ + आत्, indicating that pure आ is to be taken and not the nasal आँ ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Restored OCR-garbled Devanagari characters (आत्, आ, आँ) from vritti context.

entries.english:
366. अत् is substituted for the इ of 'pathin', 'mathin' and 'ṛbhukshin', in the strong cases.
Note:—Though the anuvṛitti of आत् was here, the separate mention of अत् is for the sake of VI. 4. 98 S. 354 by which in the case of ऋभुक्षिन् we have two forms, ऋभुक्षाणम् and ऋभुक्षणम् ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Restored dropped Devanagari 'अत्' and 'इ' in heading from sutra and vritti context.

entries.english:
367. न्थ् is substituted for the थ् of pathin and mathin, in the strong cases.
Thus पन्थाः, पन्थानौ, पन्थानः, मन्थाः, मन्थानौ, मन्थानः ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Sutra and vritti on p. 215; English heading and examples on p. 216.

entries.english:
368. The last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, is dropped in pathin, mathin, and ṛbhukshin, before an affix beginning with a vowel or य (before which the stem is called Bha I. 4. 18).
As पथः, पथा, पथे, मथः, मथा, मथे, ऋभुक्षः, ऋभुक्षा, ऋभुक्षे ॥
In the Feminine the affix ङीप् will be added by IV. 1. 5. as पथिन् + ङीप्, and the इन् is elided before the affix ङीप् by the present Sûtra. Thus सुपथी नगरी, and ऋभुक्षी सेना.
In the Neuter, there is no lengthening of VII. 1. 85. S. 365. because the affix is elided by using the word लुक् (VII. 1. 23. S. 319) and therefore the affix सु leaves no trace behind by I. 1. 63. S. 263. Thus सुपथि वनम्. Thus सुपथिन् + सु = सुपथिन् + 0 = सुपथि (The final न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7, S. 236).
In the Vocative Sing. of the Neuter Noun सुपथिन्, the elision of न् is optional, according to the following Vārtika:—
Vārtika:—In the Voc. Singular of the Neuter nouns, the elision of final न् is optional.
Thus हे सुपथिन् or हे सुपथि.
The short इ of सुपथि is not guṇated (as it is guṇated in हे हरे) because of the prohibition contained in VIII. 2. 2, S. 353 by which the elision of न् is asiddha in the case of case-endings.
In the Nom: Dual, the base being bha, the टि portion of पथिन् is elided before the Dual affix शी. Thus सुपथी ॥
In the Nom: Pl. (शि) which is a Sarvanāmasthāna affix (I. 1. 42. S. 313) there is no elision and the rules VII. 1. 86 and 87 S. 366 and 367 apply and so we get the form सुपन्थानि ॥
The Acc: forms are the same as the Nominative ones, as सुपथि, सुपथी, सुपन्थानि ॥
The Instr: Sing and Dual are सुपथा, सुपथिभ्याम् ॥
The Dative Sing: is सुपथे &c.
Now, we take up the declension of पञ्चन्. It is a षट् word by the following definition.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN
entries.note: Restored OCR-garbled and dropped Devanagari forms across pp. 216-217.

entries.english:
369. The Saṅkhyās having ष् or न् as their final are called ṣaṭ.
It is one of the peculiarities of षट् words that they lose their nominative and accusative plural terminations (VII. 1. 22. S. 261). Thus पञ्च, पञ्च ॥
Why do we say संख्या ॥ Observe विप्रुषः and पामानः ॥
Note:—This sûtra defines the term षट् which is a subdivision of the larger group saṅkhyā. Those Saṅkhyās which end in ष् or न् are called षट् । The word saṅkhyā is understood in this sûtra, because the word षट् is in the feminine gender, showing that it qualifies saṅkhyā which is also feminine.
The numerals that end in ष् or न् are six, namely पञ्चन् 'five', षष् 'six', सप्तन् 'seven', अष्टन् 'eight', नवन् 'nine', दशन् 'ten'.
The word अन्तः in the sûtra shows that the letters ष् and न् must be aupadeśika i. e., must belong to the words as originally enunciated and not added afterwards as affix &c. Thus in शतानि 'hundreds', सहस्राणि 'thousands', अष्टानाम् 'of eights' the न् is not radical, but an augment, and therefore they are not षट् and the nominative and accusative plural terminations are not elided; as शतान् + इ = शतानि &c.
In forming Nom: Pl: of शत we have शत + शि. Then we add नुम् by VII. 1. 72. S. 314. Thus we get शतानि. Here the word शत is a saṅkhyā and ends in न्. Why should not this शि be elided by VII. 1. 22. S. 261? This शि is not elided by the maxim संनिपातपरिभाषा ॥ For the maxim, see VII. 1. 13. S. 204. Because it was the presence of शि that caused the insertion of नुम् and now this न् cannot cause the destruction of its originator. Thus we get शतानि ॥ सहस्राणि is also similarly formed.
The Instr, Dative and Abl: plurals are पञ्चभिः, पञ्चभ्यः, पञ्चभ्यः respectively.
The augment नुट् is added by VII. 1. 55. S. 338 in forming the Gen. Pl: Then the following sûtra comes into operation.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN

entries.english:
370. In a stem ending in न्, the preceding vowel is lengthened before the affix नाम् ।
Thus पञ्चन् + नाम् (VII. 1. 55, S. 338) = पञ्चान् + नाम् (VI. 4. 7, S. 370) = पञ्चानाम् (न् being elided by VIII. 2. 7, S. 236). The Loc. Pl. is पञ्चसु ।
Similar is the declension of परमपञ्च । Thus N. Pl. परमपञ्च, Gen. Pl. is परमपञ्चानाम् ।
When पञ्च is a secondary member of a compound, there is neither लुक् of Sûtra VII. 1. 22, S. 261, nor the नुट् augment of VII. 1. 55, S. 338. Thus प्रियपञ्चन् is declined as Nom. प्रियपञ्चा, प्रियपञ्चानौ, प्रियपञ्चानः; Acc. प्रियपञ्चानम् ॥
Similar is the declension of सप्तन्, नवन् and दशन् । In the declension of अष्टन् the following rules apply.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english: 371. आ is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before a case-ending beginning with a consonant.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Reconstructed missing 'अष्टन् before a' where Devanagari word caused OCR omission.

entries.english:
372. After the stem अष्टा (the form assumed by अष्टन् VII. 2. 84) औश् is substituted for the ending of the Nominative and Accusative Plural.
Why have we taken the form अष्टा and not अष्ट? Observe अष्टौ तिष्ठन्ति, अष्टौ पश्य ॥ This peculiar construction of the present sûtra (अष्टाभ्यः instead of अष्टभ्यः) indicates, that the आ substitution for the न् of अष्टन् takes place in Nom. and Acc. Plural; and that it is also optional, which we infer from the jñâpaka of VI. 1. 172, S. 3718, where the word ‹?› indicates that there are two forms of ‹?›. This sûtra is, moreover, an exception by anticipation, to the sûtra VII. 1. 22, S. 261, by which the plural Nom. and Acc. endings are elided after the numerals called ‹?›. The elision of case-endings taught by II. 4. 71, S. 650, is not, however, barred by this rule; the elision taught therein will take place, whether this rule applies or not. Thus अष्टपुत्रः, अष्टभार्यः ॥
Note:—The use of ‹?› in sûtra VI. 1. 172, S. 3718 indicates that the word has two forms, and the substitution of long आ taught in VII. 2. 84, S. 371 thus becomes optional, because of this indication. Otherwise the employment of the word ‹?› would be useless, for by VII. 2. 84 which is couched in general terms, we would always end in a long vowel. There is another use of the word, namely, it makes the word with long आ (VII. 2. 84) to get also the designation of ‹?›. For if ‹?› was not to be called a ‹?›, like ‹?›, then there would be scope to the present sûtra in the case of ‹?› while it would be debarred in the case of ‹?› without long आ, by the subsequent rule VI. 1. 180 which applies to ‹?› word, and hence the employment of the word would become useless.
The regular declension is as follows:—
अष्टौ, अष्टौ, परमाष्टौ, अष्टाभिः, अष्टाभ्यः, अष्टाभ्यः, अष्टानाम्, अष्टासु ॥
When there is not the lengthening of न् of अष्टन्, that is when the base is not ‹?› then we have ‹?›, ‹?›, i.e. ‹?› is then declined like पञ्चन् ॥
When ‹?› forms a secondary member in a compound, it is declined like राजन् ॥
Thus the Acc. Pl. is प्रियाष्ट्रः ॥ The ‹?› is not changed to ‹?› because the elided अ is considered as sthânivat, because of I. 1. 57, S. 50 where the word पूर्वविधि is explained as पूर्वस्माद्विधि ॥ And as here, because of the prior (ट्) letter, the subsequent letter requires to be changed to ‹?›, the elided अ becomes sthânivat and prevents the change.
Moreover the form may be evolved by following the maxim of ‹?›; then the elision of अ of ‹?› being considered as a bahiranga for the purposes of the antaranga rule of ‹?› (VIII. 4. 41, S. 113) then also there will be no change.
Because the elision rule VI. 4. 134 applies to an operation brought about by an external cause like शस्, while the change of त् to ट् is internal, therefore the latter is antaranga to the former, and does not perceive it.
So also Ins. S. प्रियाष्ट्रा &c.
The lengthening of न in अष्टन् to आ which we have inferred in the case of अष्टन् before जस् and शस् (see above) is to take place then only when अष्टन् retains its primary sense and not when it is a secondary member in a Bahuvrîhi compound. As in the compound प्रियाष्टन् meaning "he who loves eight persons," the word प्रियाष्टन् is secondary, the principal word being the lover: therefore we do not get at all the lengthening of न in प्रियाष्टन् before जस् and शस् ॥ While there will be optional lengthening before affixes beginning with consonants. As प्रियाष्ट्रभ्याम् or प्रियाष्टाभ्याम् ॥
Verse: This word प्रियाष्टन् resembles राजन् in all the cases, except the cases beginning with a consonant where it resembles हाहा. Before consonantal cases, then the base is प्रियाष्टा ॥
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in न् ॥
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ध् ।
Now we take up the declension of बुध्. It is formed by adding the affix क्विप् to the root बुध्. The ध् is changed to भ् by VIII. 2. 37, S. 326. ध् is changed to त्, optionally to द्, by (VIII. 2. 39, S. 84). Thus N. S. is भुत् or भुद्, Nom. D. बुधौ, N. P. बुधः, Ins. S. बुधा, Ins. D. भुद्भ्याम्, Loc. Pl. भुत्सु ॥
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ध् ।
Declension of Masculine nouns ending in ज् ॥
Now we take up the declension of युज् । It is formed irregularly by adding the affix क्विन् to the root युज् by the following Sûtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Numerous corrupted/omitted Devanagari fragments in commentary and intervening prose on बुध्.

entries.english:
373. The words ऋत्विक् 'a domestic priest', दधृक् 'impudent', स्रग् 'a garland', दिग् 'direction', and उष्णिग् 'a quatrain' are irregularly formed by adding the affix क्विन्; and so also after the verbs अञ्चु 'to worship', युज् 'to join' and क्रुञ्च् 'to approach', the affix क्विन् is employed.
The affix क्विन् comes after the three roots अञ्चु, युज्, and क्रुञ्च् ॥ Being read along with the above-mentioned five irregularly-formed words, there is some irregularity in the application of क्विन् to these verbs.
The affix क्विन् comes after युज् when these are uncombined.
Note:—Otherwise in combination the affix would be क्विप् (III. 2. 61, S. 2975). The difference between क्विप् and क्विन् is that the latter gives us the Nom. S. युङ्; while the former will give us the N. S. युक् as in अश्वयुक् ॥
Of the affix क्विन् the क् and न् are indicatory (इत्); the affix is really व् ॥ This is a कृत् affix or the affix from which a nominal stem is formed directly from the verb. कृत् is defined in the following sûtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari words from clear English definitions according to Rule 2.

entries.english:
374. In this portion of the Sûtras in which there is a reference to verbal roots, any affix except तिङ् (tense-affixes), is called कृत् ॥

The Kṛit affix ‹?› is elided by the following sûtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: panini_ref printed digits read 3.1.63 (Ashtadhyayi 3.1.93)

entries.english:
375. There is elision of the affix ‹?› when reduced to the single letter ‹?› ॥

Note:—The affix ‹?› includes ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› &c. In all these, the real affix is ‹?›, which being an apṛkta (I. 2. 41 S. 251), is elided. Thus ‹?›, ‹?› (III. 2. 87 S. 2998). Here the affix क्विप् is elided. So also घृतस्पृक्, तैलस्पृक् (III. 2. 58 S. 432). Here the affix ‹?› is elided. So also अर्धभाक्, पादभाक्, तुरीभाक् (III. 2. 62 S. 2976). Here the affix ‹?› is elided.

Why do we say "of an apṛkta—an affix consisting of a single letter"?

Observe ‹?› formed by the affix ‹?› (‹?› being the real affix ‹?›); so also ‹?› formed by ‹?›, see Uṇādi Sûtras IV. 53, 44. No root can become a noun unless some kṛt affix is added to it (see I. 2. 45 and 46); hence the necessity of these imaginary affixes, in order to raise certain roots bodily, without any change, to the rank of nouns—from Dhâtu to a Prâtipadika the way lies only through an affix. And though these imaginary affixes are after all totally elided, yet by I. 1. 62, they leave their characteristic mark behind, namely, the derivative word becomes a nominal stem &c. Thus ‹?› words are adverbs (Gati) and Indeclinables.

The word ‹?› being a ‹?› word gets the designation of Prâtipadika by I. 2. 46 S. 179 and therefore we add to it the case affixes ‹?› &c. Thus ‹?› + ‹?› ॥ At this stage comes the following sûtra for application.

N. S.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
376. The nominal stem ‹?› gets before the strong cases the augment ‹?›, when it does not stand in a compound.

Thus ‹?› (the ‹?› being elided by VI. 1. 68, S. 252.) = ‹?› (the ‹?› being elided by VIII. 2. 23, S. 54).

Thus we get ‹?›.

Now applies the following sûtra.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: SK serial number misread as ३७९ in OCR, corrected to 376 by sequence

entries.english:
377. A stem formed with the affix ‹?› under III. 2. 58 &c., substitutes, at the end of a word, a guttural for the final consonant.

Note:—The word पदस्य is understood here. The word क्विन्प्रत्यय is a Bahuvrîhi meaning 'that stem which has kvin as its affix.' For the final consonant of such a stem, a guttural is substituted. As घृतस्पृक् (III. 2. 58), जलस्पृक्, मन्त्रस्पृक् ॥

The न् being changed to guttural, we get ङ्. Thus युज् + न् becomes युङ् (Nominative Singular).

In forming N. Dual the ‹?› is changed to anusvâra by VIII. 3. 24. S. 123, and this anusvâra is changed to ‹?› being the nasal letter belonging to च varga. But the anusvâra as ordained by the subsequent Tripâdî rule VIII. 3. 24. S. 123, is asiddha for the purposes of the application of VIII. 2. 30 S. 378 which required the anusvâra to be changed to guttural.

Thus युञ्जौ (N. D.), युञ्जः (N. Pl.). Acc. forms are युञ्जम्, युञ्जौ, युजः; Instr. forms are युजा, युग्भ्याम् &c.

Why do we say असमासे in the sûtra VII. 1. 71. S. 376? Because in compounds like सुयुज्, there is no नुम् augment. In declining this word the following rule applies:—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: panini_ref printed digits read 5.2.62 (Ashtadhyayi 8.2.62, cited as VIII. 2. 62 in SK 378 text)

entries.english:
378. A Guttural is substituted for a Palatal, before a jhal letter or at the end of a word.

This requires the change of ज् to a guttural i.e. of क class. The कुत्व ordained by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377 is asiddha or not perceived by the present Sûtra, which is antecedent to VIII. 2. 62. S. 377 in the order of enunciation by Pâṇini. In the case of ‹?› and ‹?›, the ‹?› is not changed to a letter of the ‹?› class even when we take words to be formed by the affix ‹?› under Sûtra VIII. 2. 62 S. 377. The reason for this we shall explain under Sûtra VIII. 2. 68. S. 443 in declining the Neuter noun.

Thus Nom. forms are सुयुक् or सुयुग्, सुयुजौ, सुयुजः ॥

In the Sûtra VII. 1. 71, S. 376, the root is exhibited as युजेः showing that that root of the Dhâtupâṭha should be taken which ends in इ, viz., the root युजिँ the 7th root of the रुधादि class. Therefore it does not apply to the root युज the 10th root of the दिवादि class and is Âtmanepadî. In the latter case, the form will be युक्.

Now we take up the declension of खन्. It is derived from खज् ‘to move' and 'to feel done up' by adding the affix ‹?› ॥

The ‹?› of ‹?› is elided because it is ‹?›, leaving behind ‹?› to which the augment ‹?› is added by VII. 1. 58. S. 2262. Thus we get ‹?›. Then ‹?› is elided by VIII. 2. 23 S. 54. In the N. S. the affix सु is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. Thus the N. S. remains as खन्. The N. Dual and Pl. are खञ्जौ and खञ्जः &c.

Now we take up the declension of राज्. By VIII. 2. 36. S. 294, the ज् of राज् is changed to ष. Then the ष is changed to ड by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84, and VIII. 4. 56. S. 206. Then ड is changed to ट. Thus we get N. S. राट् or राड्. The N. D. and Pl. are राजौ, राजः ॥ Loc. Pl. is राट्सु or राड्सु. Similarly is declined विभ्राज्. So also देवेज्. Its Nom. forms are देवेद् or देवेड्, देवेजौ, देवेजः ॥ The Nom. forms of विश्वसृज् are विश्वसृद् or विश्वसृड्, विश्वसृजौ, विश्वसृजः ॥ With regard to ‹?› and ‹?› there is not gutturalisation as will be further explained under Sûtra VIII. 2. 68. S. 443. The N. S. of परिमृज् is परिमृट् ॥

The word विभ्राज् given above is formed from that root which belongs to फणादि subdivision of भ्वादि gaṇa, i.e. the root डुभ्राज् 'to shine' भ्वादि 875, and not the root भ्राज् number 20 of the भ्वादि where it is exhibited भ्राजृ दीप्तौ. This we do, because the root भ्राज् is read along with root राज् in the subdivision; and as the VIII. 2. 36. S. 294. mentions भ्राज् and राज् together, the भ्राज् here should be taken as the भ्राज् of the फणादि class, where also both are enunciated together and not the other which is shown along with ‹?› and ‹?› (Dhâtupâṭha I. 193, 194 and 195). In the case of this भ्राज् there will be कुत्व and not षत्व. Thus N. S. is विभ्राक् or विभ्राग्. Instr. D. विभ्राग्भ्याम् &c.

Vârtika:—When व्रज् is preceded by upapada परि there comes the affix क्विप् and the ‹?› is lengthened and ज् is changed to ष when it is final in a Pada. Thus N. S. of परिव्राज् is परिव्राट् which means one who has gone out leaving every thing. The N. Dual and Pl are परिव्राजौ and परित्राजः respectively.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
Now, we take up the declension of विश्वराज्. In its declension, the following rule applies :--

379. The final vowel of विश्व is lengthened before वसु and राट् (the form assumed by राज्).

Thus विश्वावसुः, i.e. one whose wealth is the whole universe. The rule applies to the राट् form of राज् in the Nominative singular, and not when it retains its own form as विश्वराजौ, विश्वराजः ॥

The राट् is taken in the Sûtra only as an illustration of its Padânta form. It does not mean that the form विश्वाराड् is not valid. Thus N. S. has both forms, i.e. विश्वाराट् and विश्वाराड्.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN ज्
entries.note: Reconstructed OCR-corrupted Devanagari forms from clear English context.

entries.english:
Now, we take up the declension of भ्रस्ज्. In its declension the following rule applies :--

380. The स् or क्, when initial in a conjunct consonant, is dropped before a jhal affix and at the end of a word.

Thus to the root भ्रस्ज् we add the affix क्विप् and the र् is vocalised into ऋ by VI. 1. 16. S. 2412, and then the स् being elided by the present Sûtra, ज् is changed into ष् by VIII. 2. 36. S. 294, which is again changed into ट् or ड् as in the case of राट् already shown above under VIII. 2. 30. S. 378. Thus N. S. is भृट् or भृड्.

In forming N. Dual, the स् is changed to श् by VIII. 4. 40. S. 111. This is again changed to ज् by VIII. 4. 53. S. 52. Thus N. D. is भृज्जौ N. Pl. is भृज्जः.

Now we take up the declension of ऋत्विज्. This word is irregularly formed by adding the affix क्विन् to the root यज् with the upapada (subsidiary term) ऋतु in combination (See III. 2. 59. S. 373). The क्विन् formed word is finally changed to guttural by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377. Thus the N. S is ऋत्विक् or ऋत्विग्, N. D. and Plural ऋत्विजौ and ऋत्विजः ॥

Now we take up the declension of ऊर्ज्. By Sûtra VIII. 2. 24. S. 280, no consonant after र् is elided except स्. Therefore ज् is not elided, though it is the final of a conjunct consonant. Though the final ज् would have been elided even after र् by VIII. 2. 23, the special mention of स् after र् shows, that this is a niyama rule. So that any other letter than स् following after र् will not be dropped. Thus from ऊर्ज् + क्विप् (III. 2. 177. S. 3157), here ज् is not elided, though final in a pada, but is changed to a guttural by VIII. 2. 30. S. 378, and to क् by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206. Thus N. S. is ऊर्क्, ऊर्ग्. N. D. and Pl. are ऊर्जी and ऊर्जः.

Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ज्.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN ज्
entries.note: Fixed entry heading number 880 to 380; reconstructed heavily corrupted Devanagari fragments from context and citations.

entries.english:
There are no Masculine nouns ending in झ, or ञ.

We take up now the declension of त्यद्. The द् of त्यद् is replaced by अ by VII. 2. 102. S. 265. and then there is the substitution of the form of the subsequent by VI. 1. 97. S. 191. Thus we get the base त्य before the case affixes.

In forming the Nom. Sing, the following rule applies :--

381. For the non-final त् and द् of त्यद् &c. there is substituted स in the Nominative Singular.

As त्यद् + सु = त्य + अ + सु (VII. 2. 102) = स्य + अ + सु (VII. 2. 106) = स्यः (VI. 1. 97). Similarly सः from तद्, एषः from एतद् as एतद् + सु = एत + अ + स् (VII. 2. 102) = एष + अ + स् (VII. 2. 106) = एषः (VI. 1. 97). So असौ from अदस् by the sûtra VII. 2. 107. Why do we say 'non-final'? Observe ‹?› ॥ Had not this word been used, the case-affix would not be elided in the vocative, as then there would have been no short vowel, as required by VI. 1. 69. S. 193.

This rule only applies to त्यदादि words, which as we have already shown, begin with त्यद् and end with द्वि in the list of sarvanâmas. Therefore this will not apply to त्वम् which is not included in the त्यदादि class.

Nor should it be stated that "this rule could not have applied to the त् of त्वम्, for if it did so, what was the necessity of teaching त्व substitution in the place of युष्मद् by VII. 2. 94 S. 384. That sûtra could have been made as त्वम् instead of त्वामौ, for it would have been better to say at once let त्वम् be the N. S. of युष्मद्, instead of first making it त्व and then changing the form into त्वम्" ॥ To this argument we reply, that the rule of त् substitution will find its unrestricted scope in words like अतित्वम्, where युष्मद् is a secondary member only. In the case of त्वम् the present rule would have applied. When these words i. e. त्यद् &c. are used as proper nouns or sanjnâs (संज्ञा) or when used as secondary members of a compound, the rules of VII. 2. 102 S. 265 and VII. 2. 106 S. 381. will not apply because they are sarvanâmas, for see explanation under sûtra I. 1. 29. S. 222. Thus त्यद्, त्यदौ, त्यदः ; अतित्यत्, अतित्यौ, अतित्यदः &c.

The pronoun यद् is declined as यः, यौ, ये ॥ एतद् is declined as एषः, एतौ, एते ॥

In re-employment or अन्वादेश for which, see II. 4. 34. S. 351. we have Acc forms एनम्, एनौ, एनान्, Instr: Sg. एनेन; Genitive and Loc: Dual एनयोः ॥

entries.english:
Now we take up the declension of युष्मद् and अस्मद्. In its declension, the following rules apply :--

382. अम् is substituted for the Dative case-affix ङे and for the endings of the Nominative and Accusative in all numbers, after the stems युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥

Note:—The ङे the ending of the Dative is exhibited anomalously in the sûtra without any case ending (compare VII. 1. 13, ङेर्यः) प्रथमयोः means 'of the first and second cases'.

Thus युष्मद् + ङे = तुभ्यद् + ङे (VII. 2. 95) = तुभ्य + ङे (VII. 2. 90) = तुभ्य + अम् (VII. 1. 28) = तुभ्यम् (VI. 1. 107 or 97); similarly मह्यम् ॥
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI

entries.english:
Then the rule after the following applies, to understand which the following rule is necessary.

383. The substitutions taught hereafter upto VII. 2. 98 take effect with regard to the portions of युष्मद् and अस्मद् upto म् ie the substitutes replace युष्म and अस्म ||

This is an Adhikâra Sûtra and exerts governing influence on all the seven subsequent sûtras in the order of Ashțâdhyâyî.

entries.english: 384. In the Nominative Singular त्व is substituted for युष्म and अह for अस्मद् ॥

entries.english:
385. In the remaining cases where (आ or य is not substituted by VII. 2. 88. and 89. S. 387, 392.) there is elision of the final of yushmad and asmad.

Thus युष्मद् + सु = युष्मद् + अम् (VII. 1. 28. S. 342) = त्वद् (VII. 2. 94. S. 384) + अम् = त्व + अम् (द् is elided by the present sûtra) = त्वम् (by VI. 1. 97. S. 191, and VI. 1. 107. S. 194). Similarly, the N. S. of अस्मद् is अहम् ॥

Why is not टाप् added in the feminine in 'त्वं स्त्री' 'अहं स्त्री'? For त्व + अम् and अह + अम् the pûrvarûpa rule ordained by VI. 1. 97. S. 191 and VI. 1. 107. S. 194, though subsequent, is after all bahiranga, and would be set aside by the antaranga rule ordaining टाप् to be added to त्व and अह?

True. But युष्मद् and अस्मद् have no genders, and therefore they have no feminine forms and consequently would not give occasion to the addition of the affix टाप्.

Or, in order to avoid all this difficulty about टाप्, some would elide the अद् (or remaining portion) of युष्मद् and अस्मद् under this sûtra. They argue that by the previous sûtra VII. 2. 91. S. 383 the portions 'yushm' and 'asm', namely the portions upto म of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are replaced by substitutes. The portion that remains (शेष) is अद्, and it is this अद् which is to be elided.

According to their view, the word शेष does not refer to the vibhakti or case affix, but the force of Locative in शेषे is that of a genitive, meaning “of the remaining” and to point out the particular sthânî which is to be replaced. Therefore in युष्मद् and अस्मद्, the युष्म् and अस् portions have been already operated upon by other rules, the द् that remains is a portion.

In this view, the Sûtra should be translated as "in the remaining cases (i. e. where आ is not substituted as by VII. 2. 88. S. 387, nor य as by VII. 2. 89. S. 392) there is elision of the remaining (अद्) portion (I. 1. 64. S. 79) of these two (युष्मद् and अस्मद्)".

In the feminine, there is one more point to be considered even in the light of the second explanation. In युष्मद् + अम् = त्व + अद् + अम् if we follow the ordinary rule of ‹?› the अद् should be elided first by शेषे लोपः; then should apply the rule of अतो गुणे if at all. Then the form will be त्व + अम् ॥ Here त्व ends with अ, and so would require टाप् in the feminine, and the same difficulty again recurs. To clear up this point, we state that the rule of elision (शेषे लोपः) is bahiranga, because its efficient cause lies outside in the affix अम्, while the अतो गुणे rule is antaranga, because the occasion for its application or the efficient cause is within the very form त्व + अद्. Therefore अतो गुणे will apply first, we get त्वद् + अम्. Then शेषे लोपः produces its effect i. e. अद् is elided, and we get त्व् + अम् ॥ As there is no अ in त्व्, it would not require टाप् ॥ Thus we get त्वम् in the feminine also.

So also परमत्वम्, परमाहम्, अतित्वम् and अत्यहम्. In forming the N. Dual, the following rules apply.

entries.english:
387. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before the ending of the Nom. Du. in the spoken language.

As युवाम्, आवाम् ॥ It would have been better had the Sûtra been enunciated as “औङि” only. Why in the “spoken language”? Observe युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे in the Veda, so also आवाम् ॥

Why 'upto म'? Observe युवकाम्, आवकाम् ॥ The क (V. 3. 71. S. 2026), is not replaced. Similarly VII. 2. 97. S. 389 teaches that त्व and म replace 'yushmad' and 'asmad' in the singular; by the sûtra VII. 2. 91. S. 383 'yushm' and 'asm' are only replaced. Thus त्वया, मया the अद् portion remains for which य is substituted by VII. 2. 89. S. 392. Had the whole been replaced, then the अ of त्व and म would have been replaced by य (VII. 2. 89. S. 392), and given us undesired forms like त्या and म्या ॥ Similarly the forms युवकाभ्याम् and आवकाभ्याम् would not have been evolved.

In forming the N. Pl. the following rule applies.

entries.english:
388. In the Nom. Pl. यूय is substituted for युष्मद्, and वय for अस्मद् ॥

Thus यूयम्, वयम्, परमयूयम्, परमवयम्, अतियूयम्, अतिवयम् ॥

Now some one may object that जस् (Nom. Pl.) should be changed into शी (VII. 1. 17. S. 214); after त् in युष्मत् has been elided by शेषे लोपः in the first sense; for then the base is युष्म which ends in अ which is the efficient cause for the application of जसः शी rule. To this we reply, that the following maxim prevents this incongruity:

Maxim:— If one sûtra of the Angâdhikâra (VI. 4. 1. to VII. 4. end) has once been applied, another sûtra of the same Adhikâra is not subsequently applicable.

Therefore जस् is not replaced by शी. Or we may say that in the sûtra ङे प्रथमयोरम् (VII. 1. 28. S. 382) one more म् is understood, i. e. the sûtra is ङे प्रथमयोरम्म्, which म् indicates that अम् will not be changed into any other form, but will remain always as अम् ending in म्.

390. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before the endings of the Accusative.

As त्वाम्, माम्, युवाम्, आवाम् ॥

entries.english:
391. न् is substituted for the श of शस् the affix of the Accusative Plural after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥

'न्' has been exhibited in the sûtra without any case affix. Thus युष्मद् + शस् = युष्म + न् + स् = युष्मा + न् (the स् is elided by संयोगान्तस्य लोपः VIII. 2. 23. S. 54 and अ is lengthened by VII. 2. 87. S. 390). The substitute replaces the initial of शस् on the maxim आदेः परस्य I. 1. 54. S. 44 because the operation is ordained after युष्मद्. Thus युष्मान् and अस्मान् ॥ This debars अम् (VII. 1.

392. य is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before a case-ending, which is not a substitute, and which begins with a vowel.
Thus त्वया, मया, त्वयि, मयि, युवयोः, आवयोः ॥

entries.english:
393. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before a case-ending, beginning with a consonant, when it is not a substitute.
The substitute case-endings are given in VII. 1. 27-33. S. 399 &c.
Thus युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम्, युष्माभिः, अस्माभिः ॥

entries.english:
394. In the Dative Singular तुभ्य is substituted for युष्म and मह्य for अस्म ॥
The affix अम् is substituted for ङे by VII. 1. 28. S. 382 the तू is elided by VII. 2. 90. S. 385.
Thus तुभ्यम्, मह्यम्, परमतुभ्यम्, परममह्यम्, अतितुभ्यम्, अतिमह्यम्, युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम् ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN ष्

entries.english:
395. भ्यम् or अभ्यम् is substituted for the Dative भ्यस् after 'yushmad' and 'asmad.'
As युष्मभ्यम् and अस्मभ्यम् ॥ As the sutra is constructed (भ्यसोऽभ्यम्), it is not easy to say whether the substitute is भ्यम् or अभ्यम् ॥ If it is भ्यम्, then we have two cases, (1) eliding the final द् of yushmad and asmad, by VII. 2. 90. S. 385 and adding भ्यम् (2) eliding अद् of yushmad and asmad by VII. 2. 90, and adding भ्यम् ॥ It has been already shown in S. 385 that VII. 2. 90, is capable of two explanations, one by which yushmad and asmad lose their द् only, and by another अद् ॥ Similarly with अभ्यम् we have also two cases. Thus we have four cases, as (1) yushma+bhyam, (2) yushm+bhyam, (3) yushma+abhyam, (4) yushm+abhyam. In the case of the first (yushma+bhyam) we can get the proper form, though it may be objected that yushma+bhyam should be equal to ‹?› by VII. 3. 103. S. 205. This ए substitution will not take place, however, by force of the maxim अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिर्निष्ठितस्य 'when an operation which is taught in the angâdhikâra has taken place, and another operation of the angadhikara is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place.'
The second case is an impossibility, namely, yushm+bhyam can give us no form. The third case yushma+abhyam will give us the proper form युष्मभ्यम् (अ+अ=अ by VI. 1. 97 S. 191). Moreover the accent also will be on the middle by VI. 1. 161, the udâtta अ of yushma being elided by the anudâtta of अभ्यम्, the acute will be on the anudâtta. It should not be objected that in VI. 1. 161, the word of VI. 1. 159 S. 3680 is understood, and the accent will be on the final. We shall show in that sutra, that the udâtta will fall on the आदि (beginning) of the anudâtta term which causes the elision.
The fourth alternative yushm+abhyam is free from all objections.

396. This substitution of अत् is made in the singular number also of the Ablative, after yushmad and asmad.
As त्वत् and मत्. For the substitution of त्व and म see VII. 2. 97; S. 389, and त्व + अत् = त्वत् and म + अत् = मत् by VI. 1. 97. S. 191.
It would have been better to have enunciated the Sutra as 'पञ्चम्येकवचनस्य'.
Abl. Dual युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम्.
