entries.english:
397. अत् is substituted for the Ablative भ्यस् after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥
As युष्मत्, अस्मत् ॥
The द् is elided by VII. 2. 90. S. 385 before the case-ending भ्यस् and युष्म + अत् = युष्मत् by VI. 1. 97. S. 191.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN ष्

entries.english: 398. In the Genitive Singular तव is substituted for युष्म and मम for अस्म ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN ष्

entries.english:
399. अश् (I. 1. 55), is substituted for the Genitive ending ङस् after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥
Thus तव and मम; युवयोः, आवयोः ॥
The indicatory श् of अश् shows that by I. 1. 55, S. 45 the whole of the affix ङस् is to be replaced: otherwise it would have replaced only the first letter of the affix and the affix not being a substitute-affix, rule VII. 2. 89 S. 392 would not be applicable to it. The तव is substituted for युष्मद् and मम for अस्मद् by VII. 2. 96 S. 398 and तव + अ (अश्), and मम + अ = तव and मम by VI. 1. 97. S. 191.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN ष्

entries.english:
400. आकम् is substituted for the Genitive plural affix साम् (VII. 1. 52 S. 217.), after yushmad, and asmad.
साम् is the affix आम् of the Genitive plural with the augment सुट् । Thus युष्माकम् and अस्माकम् । Why is it read साम् and not आम्, when there is no स
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN ष्

entries.english:
at the time when the substitution is ordained? It is read as ‹?› in order to indicate that ‹?› will not get the augment ‹?›, for otherwise 'yushma' and 'asma' having lost their 'd' by VII. 2. 90, S. 385 end in ‹?›, and so by VII. 1. 52, S. 217 would cause the genitive affix to get the augment ‹?›; the present Sûtra removes that also. The substitute is exhibited with a long ‹?›, in order to make अ + आ = आ in युष्म + आकम्, had it been short अ, then there would have been no lengthening, but ‹?› by VI. 1. 97. S. 191. If you say 'the very fact that आकम् was taught and not कम् would prevent para-rupa and cause lengthening'; we reply, that the ‹?› of आकम् would find its scope in preventing ‹?› substitution. For without आ, we should have युष्म + कम् = युष्मकम् (VII. 3. 103 S. 205).

Why has Pânini used the form सामः and not आमः? The objector may say there was no necessity of using सामः for the following reason :— as the base युष्मत् ends in a consonant, the sûtra आमि सर्वनाम्नः सुट् (VII. 1. 52 S. 217) cannot apply here, as its efficient cause (i. e. an anga ending in a vowel) is absent. We reply to this, that after the elision of ‹?› by (VII. 2. 90. S. 385) the सुट् will come, because then the base ends in a vowel. To remove that सुट्, Pânini has stated सामः आकम् ॥

But when the sûtra ‹?› is taken in the second sense, there is no necessity of inserting सामः in the present sûtra, as in that case, the base will end in a consonant whereby the sûtra सर्वनाम्नः सुट् is prevented.

Verses:— When युष्मद् and अस्मद् denoting a unity or a duality in themselves are members of a compound, which may denote any number, then also ‹?› and ‹?›, and ‹?› and ‹?› will be substituted for युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥ (1)

But when they are followed by सु (Nom. S.), जस् (Nom. Pl.), ङे (Dat. S.), ङस् (Gen. S.), then युष्मद् will be replaced by त्व, यूय, तुभ्य and तव and अस्मद् by अह, वय, मह्य and मम ॥ (2)

Now these supersede ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?› by being taught subsequently to the rule teaching ‹?› and ‹?› substitutions. While ‹?› and ‹?› are superseded by the above, by the rule of पूर्वविप्रतिषेध ॥ (3)

When the compound denotes a singular or a dual number, and the component members युष्मद् and अस्मद् denote a plural number, then युव, आव, ‹?› and ‹?› will not be substituted for them, as the efficient cause (one-ness or duality) is wanting here. (4)

I. युष्मद् AND अस्मद् [SINGULAR].

Now we take अतित्वम् and अत्यहम् ॥ When these compounds are analysed, they stand thus अतिक्रान्तः त्वाम् = अतित्वम्, अतिक्रान्तः माम् = अत्यहम् ॥ Here the component parts युष्मद् and अस्मद् denote singular number, and the whole compound means a third person. The compound is thus formed अति + युष्मद् = अतियुष्मद् and so also अति अस्मद् ॥ These are dvitiya Tatpurusha compounds and consequently they get Pratipadika samjna and सु in the Nom. S. Thus अतियुष्मद् + सु ॥ Here the component member युष्मद् denotes a singular, and the compound itself is followed by सु, and so the rule contained in the second verse applies : and we have अतित्वम् and अत्यहम् ॥

Now we take up अतियुष्मद् + औ (Nom. Dual) = अतियुष्मद् + आम् (प्रथमाद्वितीययोश्च VII. 1. 28 S. 382). Here the rule contained in the first verse applies, so we get अतित्व + आम् = अतित्वाम्. So also अतिमाम् ॥

Then अतियुष्मद् + जस् ॥ Here the second verse will apply, and we have अतियूय + अम् = अतियूयम् ॥ So also अतिवयम् ॥

Then in Acc. Sing and Dual we have अतित्वाम् and अतिमाम् by the first verse. In Acc. Pl. we have अतित्वान् and अतिमान् by the same.

The Ins. forms are derived by applying the first verse : as अतित्वया, अतित्वाभ्याम्, अतित्वाभिः &c. In the Dative Sing. the second verse will apply and thus we get अतितुभ्यम् and अतिमह्यम् ॥ In the remaining numbers of the Dative, the first rule will apply.

In the Ablative, the first verse will apply as अतित्वत् (S), अतित्वाभ्याम् (D), अतित्वाभ्यः (Pl.)

In the Gen. S. the second verse will apply, and so we get अतितव and अतिमम ॥ In the remaining numbers the first verse will apply.

In the Locative Sing., Dual and Plural the first verse will apply.

II. युष्मद् AND अस्मद् IN THE DUAL.

When the compounds अतियुष्मद् and अत्यस्मद् are analysed as अतिक्रान्तः युवाम् and अतिक्रान्तः आवाम्, then :—

अतियुष्मद् + सु = अतित्व + अम् = अतित्वम् and so also अत्यहम् ॥ Here the second verse will apply. In the Nom. Dual the first verse will apply, and we get ‹?› and ‹?› ॥ In the Nom. Pl., the second verse will apply, and we have अतियूयम् and अतिवयम् ॥

In all numbers of the Acc. the first verse will apply as अतियुवाम्, and अतियुवाम् and अत्यावाम् and अत्यावाम् ॥ In the plural we have अतियुवान् and अत्यावान् ॥

In the Ins. numbers the first verse will apply : and we have अतियुवया अतियुवाभ्याम् and अतियुवाभिः; and अत्यावया अत्यावाभ्याम् and अत्यावाभिः ॥

In the Dative Sing. the second verse will apply and we have अतितुभ्यम् and अतिमह्यम्. The dual and plural are formed by the first verse : as अतियुवाभ्याम् and अतियुवभ्यम् and अत्यावाभ्याम् and अत्यावभ्यम् ॥

In the Ablative, the first verse applies : as अतियुवत्, अतियुवाभ्याम् and अतियुवभ्यम् and अत्यावत्, अत्यावाभ्याम् and अत्यावभ्यम् ॥

In the Gen. S. the second verse will apply and in the Dual and Plural the first : and we have : अतितव, अतियुवयोः अतियुवाकम् ॥ So also अतिमम, अत्यावयोः and अत्यावाकम् ॥

In the Loc. Sing. Dual and Pl. the first verse will apply and so we get :— अतियुवयि, अतियुवयोः, अतियुवासु ॥ So also अत्यावयि, अत्यावयोः and अत्यावासु ॥

III. युष्मद् and अस्मद् in the Plural.

When युष्मद् and अस्मद् denote plural: as अतिक्रान्तः युष्मान् or अस्मान् ॥ Here the fourth verse will apply, and अतियुष्मद् and अति-अस्मद् will be declined as follows :—

Nom. Acc. Ins. Dat. Abl. Gen. Loc.
Singular अतियूयम् अतियुष्माम् अतियुष्मया अतितुभ्यम् अतियुष्मत् अतितव अतियुष्मयि
Dual अतियुष्माम् अतियुष्माम् अतियुष्माभ्याम् अतियुष्माभ्याम् अतियुष्माभ्याम् अतियुष्मयोः अतियुष्मयोः
Plural अतियूयम् अतियुष्मान् अतियुष्माभिः अतियुष्मभ्यम् अतियुष्मत् अतियुष्माकम् अतियुष्मासु
अत्यहम् अत्यस्माम् अत्यस्मया अतिमह्यम् अत्यस्मत् अतिमम अत्यस्मयि
अत्यस्माम् अत्यस्माम् अत्यस्माभ्याम् अत्यस्माभ्याम् अत्यस्माभ्याम् अत्यस्मयोः अत्यस्मयोः
अतिवयम् अत्यस्मान् अत्यस्माभिः अत्यस्मभ्यम् अत्यस्मत् अत्यस्माकम् अत्यस्मासु
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 400 from page 232; contains heavily corrupted Devanagari fragments in verses and declension paradigms.

entries.english:
401. Upto VIII. 3. 54, inclusive, should be always supplied in every subsequent sutra, the phrase "of a word," or "to the whole of a word."

Note:—This is an adhikara sutra, and extends up to VIII. 3. 55, in order of enunciation of Pânini's Ashtâdhyâyî.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english: 402. Upto VIII. 1. 68, inclusive should always be supplied the phrase "after a pada."
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english: 403. Upto VIII. 1. 74, inclusive is to be supplied the phrase “The whole is unaccented, if it does not stand at the beginning of the foot of a verse”
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
404. For the Genitive, Dative and Accusative Dual of yushmad and asmad are substituted वाम् and नौ respectively, when a word precedes it and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta.

All the three sûtras पदस्य, पदात् and अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ are applicable here.

Note:—These two वाम् and नौ come in the Dual only, because other substitutes have been taught for the Singular and Plural in the two subsequent sûtras.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI.

entries.english: 405. For (the Genitive, Dative, and Accusative) plural of yushmad and asmad are substituted वस् and नस् respectively, (when a word precedes, and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta).\n\nThis Sûtra debars the substitutes वाम् and नौ taught in the previous Sûtra.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI.

entries.english: 406. For the Genitive and Dative Singular (of yushmad and asmad are substituted) ते and मे respectively, (when a word precedes and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse and these are anudâtta).
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI.

entries.english:
407. For the Accusative Singular of yushmad and asmad are substituted त्वा and मा respectively, under the same circumstances.

Verses.—"May the Lord of Śrî preserve thee (twâ) and me (mâ) also; here may He give to thee (te), and to me (me) also, felicity!
That Hari is thy (te) Lord and mine (me) also.
May the Omnipresent preserve you two (vâm) and also us two (nau).
May God give felicity to you two (vâm) and to us two (nau).
Hari is the Lord of you two (vâm) and also of us two (nau).
May He preserve you (vaḥ) and us (naḥ), may He give prosperity to you (vaḥ) and to us (naḥ).
He is the object of worship here of you (vaḥ) and of us (naḥ)."

Why do we say "पदात्" i. e. after a Pada? So that the substitutions may not take place when pronouns are in the beginning of a sentence. As त्वां पातु and not त्वा पातु. Similarly मां पातु also.

Why do we say "अपादादौ" i. e. when not at the beginning of a hemistich? Observe वेदरशेषैः संवेद्योऽस्मान् कृष्णः सर्वदावतु ॥ Here we have अस्मान् and not नः ॥

The word स्थ in the sûtra indicates that the case affixes must be express and not understood, for the purposes of this substitution. Therefore, not here: इति युष्मत्पुत्रो ब्रवीति । इत्यस्मत्पुत्रो ब्रवीति ॥ though here yushmat is preceded by a word in a sentence, and is in the Genitive case, yet वस् substitution (VIII. 1. 21) does not take place, because the case-affix is elided.

Vârt:—The rules relating to nighâta (by which all syllables of a word become unaccented, such as VIII. 1. 19 and VIII. 1. 28 &c) and to the substitutes of yushmad and asmad apply then only, when the preceding word which would cause the nighâta or the substitution, is part of the same sentence with the latter word. The word वाक्य or "sentence" means that which contains one finite verb. Therefore not here:—ओदनं पच तव भविष्यति । ओदनं पच, मम भविष्यति ॥ "Cook the food, it will be for thee. Cook the food, it will be for me.". That is, the rice cooked by thee, will do both for thyself and myself. Here the ते and मे substitutions have not taken place (VIII. 1. 22) for yushmad and asmad. But the rule will apply here—शालीनां ते ओदनं दास्यामि ॥ In the last example, the verb and the substitutes of yushmad and asmad are not in syntactical construction with the words that immediately precede them, and yet the substitution takes place, in spite of the general maxim समर्थः पदविधिः (II. 1. 1), for rules relating to completed words apply to such words only which are in construction.

For शालीनां is not in construction with ते, but with ओदनं i. e. शालीनां ओदनं ते दास्यामि ॥ Yet it causes substitution of yushmad. Though the preceding words are not samartha with regard to the words that follow them, they cause the changes, because the words are in the same sentence.

Vârt:—It should be stated, that the substitutes, &c. are all optional, when not employed in anvâdeśa, whether the nominative is preceded by another noun or not; but when there is anvâdeśa, then the substitution is compulsory and not optional. Thus धाता ते भक्तोऽस्ति or धाता तव भक्तोऽस्ति । But in anvâdeśa, we have only one form, as तस्मै ते नमः ॥. Which means "Brahmâ is Thy (or ‹?›) worshipper." But in the sequel, "to Thee (ते) that art such, our reverence is due," the form alone is admissible.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI.
entries.note: Sutra and vritti appear at the bottom of p. 236; English translation heading begins on p. 237; embedded Devanagari reconstructed from context.

entries.english:
408. The above substitutions do not take place, when there is in connection with the pronouns, any of these five, viz:—च, 'and'; वा, 'or'; ह, 'oh!'; अह, 'wonderful!'; or एव, 'only'.

Thus हरिस्त्वां च मां रक्षतु ॥ कथं त्वां मां वा न रक्षेत् &c.

The word युक्त is employed in the sûtra to indicate direct conjunction. Therefore, where the conjunction is not direct, but intermediate, the employment would be of the shorter forms. Thus हरो हरिश्च मे स्वामी ॥ Here the word च connects हर and हरि and not the pronoun in the above word. Therefore the prohibition does not apply.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI.
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari fragments restored from plain context.

entries.english: 409. The above substitutions do not take place also in connection with verbs having the sense of "seeing" when physical seeing is not denoted, but "knowing" is meant.\n\nNote:—The word पश्यार्थाः is equivalent to दर्शनार्थाः, and दर्शन means 'knowledge', i. e. verbs denoting 'to know'. आलोचन means perception obtained through sight i. e. physical 'seeing' opposed to metaphorical "seeing" or "knowing". The substitutions of त्वा and मा &c. for युष्मद् and अस्मद् do not take place when these pronouns are employed in connection with verbs denoting 'seeing' (metaphorically) but not 'looking' (physically).
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI.
entries.note: Sutra serial number misprinted as 402 in scan; entry cut off at bottom of page 238.

entries.english:
Thus तथा त्वां समीक्षते भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति ॥ Why do we say when not meaning 'to look'? Observe भक्तस्त्वा पश्यति चक्षुषा ॥
Ishti :—With regard to verbs of "Seeing" the rule should apply even where the connection is not direct : as,
भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN द्
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 409 from preceding page.

entries.english:
410. When the pronoun follows after a Nominative which itself is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions may take place optionally even in anvâdesa.
Thus भक्तस्त्वमप्यहं तेन हरिस्त्वां त्रायते स माम् ॥ Here the alternative forms त्वा and मा are admissible.
We have already said that युष्मद् and अस्मद् substitutions do not take place when they are in the beginning of a pada. To this, however, there is an exception, when the first word is a Vocative, technically called आमन्त्रित which is defined in the next sutra, then also though युष्मद् and अस्मद् may not really be in the beginning of a pada, yet the substitutions will not take place by the sûtra after next.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN द्

entries.english: 411. The word ending with the first case-affix, in the sense of addressing, is called Amantrita or Vocative.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN द्

entries.english:
412. A preceding Vocative is considered as non-existent, (for the purposes of the accent of the following word, and the enclitic forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्) ||
Thus अग्ने ! तव ॥ देव ! अस्मान्पाहि ॥ अग्ने ! नय ॥ अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! ॥ Here तव and अस्मान् cannot get the shorter form, though they are not at the beginning of a hemistich, because they are preceded by the आमन्त्रित words अग्ने and देव ||
Similarly in अग्ने नय the verb नय does not become accentless as it would otherwise have become by VIII. 1. 28. S. 3935.
In अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! the rule VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654 does not apply.
Note:—Such a Vocative is treated as if not at all existing, it is simply ignored. The operation which its presence otherwise would have caused does not take place, and that operation takes place which would have taken place had it not existed. What are the particular purposes served by considering it as non-existent? They are (1) the absence of the accent-less-ness of the subsequent Vocative which the first, taken as a पद, would have caused under VIII. 1. 19. S. 3654. As देवदत्त ! यज्ञदत्त ! Here the first Vocative देवदत्त does not cause the second Vocative to lose its accent, but it remains first acute by VI. 1. 198. S. 3653. (2) The accent-less-ness of the verb required by VIII. 1. 28 S. 3935 is prevented : as, देवदत्त पचसि ॥ (3) The substitution of the shorter forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्, required by VIII. 1. 20-28 S. 404 &c. is prevented, as देवदत्त तव (not ते) ग्रामः स्वम्, देवदत्त मम (not मे) ग्रामः । (4) The application of VIII. 1. 37. S. 3944 takes place, in spite of the intervention of the Vocative between the Particle and the verb; such intervention is not considered as taking away anything from the immediateness (व्यवधान) of the Particle from the verb : as, अहो देवदत्त पचसि ॥ (5) For the purposes of VIII. 1. 47, S. 3954 though a Vocative may precede, the latter is still considered as non-existent and VIII. 1. 47 applies, as देवदत्त जातु पचसि । (6) So also in the case of VIII. 1. 49, S. 3956 as अहो देवदत्त पचसि, अहो देवदत्त जल्पसि, no option is allowed here by VIII. 1. 50. S. 3957.
In 'सर्वदा रक्ष देव नः' although the word देव is non-existent, yet taking रक्ष as a preceding word, नः is used.
In इमं मे गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि the first Vocative गङ्गे is considered as non-existent with regard to मे, and, therefore, यमुने is considered as following immediately after the pada मे and thus यमुने becomes anudâtta, not because of गङ्गे, but because of मे. In other words, the intervention of the Vocatives does not stop the action of मे. This nighâta or accentlessness is heard in Pada-Pâtha only, i. e. when the words are read separately, and not in Sanhitâ-reading. In Sanhitâ there will be eka-sruti of I. 2. 39 S. 3668.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN द्
entries.note: Reconstructed dropped/mangled Devanagari words in commentary from clear context and Sanskrit vritti.

entries.english:
413. A preceding Vocative, when it conveys a general idea, is not to be considered as if non-existent, for the purposes of the subsequent Vocative, which stands in apposition with the former.
Thus हरे दयालो नः पाहि "O Hari ! O Merciful! protect us." अग्ने तेजस्विन् "O Agni! O powerful!" Here दयालो is all anudâtta by VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654, because it is preceded by a word, though that word is Vocative.
Note:—Why do we say सामान्यवचनम् 'which is a generic word'? The rule will not apply when the Vocatives are synonyms. Thus ‹?› All these Vocatives are synonyms of Saraswati, and hence all retain their accent of the Vocative (VI. 1. 198). According to Padamanjari the reading given in Taittirîya Br. is :— ‹?› सामान्यवचनम् means 'a generic term'. When the first is a generic term, and the second is a specific term, (विशेषवचन) qualifying the first, and both are in the singular number, there the present rule will apply.
This sutra prevents the operation of the last sûtra in the particular case when the two Vocatives are in apposition, and the second qualifies the first. Thus अग्ने गृहपते, माणवक जटिलकाध्यापक ॥ The first vocative being considered as existing, the second vocative loses its accent.
Why do we say 'the vocative subsequent'? Observe देवदत्त पचसि here the verb does not lose its accent. Why do we say 'standing in apposition or सामानाधिकरण्ये'?
Observe देवदत्त पण्डित यज्ञदत्त, here the word पण्डित qualifies यज्ञदत्त, and is not in apposition with देवदत्त, and hence it retains its accent.
Then applies Sûtra VIII. 1. 74. S. 3655 which for the sake of convenience we repeat here.

४१३ (क) । विभाषितं विशेषवचने । ८ । १ । ७४ ॥
अत्र भाष्यम् । बहुवचनमिति वक्ष्यामीति । बहुवचनान्तं विशेष्यं समानाधिकरणे आमन्त्रिते विशेषणे परे अविद्यमानवद्वा । यूयं प्रभवः । देवाः शरण्याः । युष्मान् भजे वो भजे इति वा । इहान्वादेशेऽपि वैकल्पिका आदेशाः । सुपात् । सुपाद । सुपादौ । सुपादः । सुपादम् । सुपादौ ।

413. A. When the preceding Vocative is in the plural number, it is optionally considered as non-existent, if the subsequent Vocative, in apposition with it, is a specific term.
Here the author of the Mahabhashya states :— "The word bahuvachanam should be added to the sûtra to complete the sense." That is the sûtra should run as विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् ॥ We have therefore translated the sûtra with this emendation of Patanjali.
Thus यूयं प्रभवः, देवाः शरण्याः । युष्मान् भजे or वो भजे ॥ Here even in anvâdesa there is optional substitution of वः for युष्मान् ॥
Now, we take up the declension of सुपाद्. In the strong, i. e. in the first five cases it is declined as :—
Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom : सुपात् or सुपाद, सुपादौ सुपादः
Ac. सुपादम्, सुपादौ.
In the formation of the Acc. Pl. and the rest, the following rule applies.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN द्
entries.note: Includes parenthetical 413 (क) / 413. A within 413 per Rule 4.

entries.english:
414. For पाद् is substituted पद् when the former is Bha.
Note:—The substitute replaces the whole form पाद् and not only the final, on the maxim निर्दिश्यमानस्यादेशा भवन्ति "substitutes take the place of that which is actually enunciated in a rule."
Thus the Acc. Pl. is सुपदः ॥
Instr: Sing and Dual are सुपदा, सुपाद्भ्याम् &c.
Now we take up the declension of अग्निमथ् meaning 'kindling fire'. It is declined as:
Nom. Sing. अग्निमत् or अग्निमद् Dual अग्निमथौ Pl. अग्निमथः
Instr: Dual is अग्निमद्भ्याम् &c.
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in थ.
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in च्.
Now we take up the declension of प्राञ्च्.
According to Sūtra III. 2. 59. S. 373, the affix क्विन् is employed after the verb अञ्च् to make it a Prātipadika, before the case terminations.
Thus having got the noun प्राञ्च्, in its declension, the following rules apply.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI. DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Word 'Bha.' in heading was displaced before entry number in OCR; table and embedded Devanagari restored.

entries.english:
415. In a root-stem ending in a consonant preceded by न्,—this न not being added to the root owing to its having an indicatory इ (VII. 1. 58)—the न is elided when an affix having an indicatory क or ङ् follows.
By Sūtra VII. 1. 70. S. 361, the stem अञ्च् gets the augment नुम् in the strong cases.
Then by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54, the last consonant is dropped. By VIII. 2. 62. S. 377, which says that 'a stem formed with the affix क्विन् substitutes at the end of a word, a guttural for the final consonant' we get the N. S. as प्राङ् thus:—
प्राञ्च् + सु = प्राच् (VI. 4. 24 S. 415) + सु = प्रा + न् (VII. 1. 70. S. 361) + च् + सु = प्रान् च् + ० (सु is elided by VI. 1. 68 S. 252) = प्रान् च् = प्रान् (च् being elided by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54) = प्राङ् (न् turned to ङ् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377).
The N. Dual &c. are formed by changing the न into anuswāra, and then the anuswāra into ञ् by VIII. 4. 58. S. 124.
Thus प्राञ्चौ प्राञ्चः Acc. प्राञ्चम्, प्राञ्चौ.
In forming the Acc. Pl. &c. the following rules apply.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI. DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
416. The अ of अच् (when अञ्च् loses its nasal,) is elided at the end of a Bha stem.
The lengthening of the first member takes place by VI. 3. 138: S. 417.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI. DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
417. The final vowel of the preceding member is lengthened before अच, when it assumes the form च, having lost its nasal and the vowel अ ॥
Thus Acc: Pl is प्राचः; Instr: Sing or Dual are प्राचा, प्राग्भ्याम् &c.
Now we take up the declension of प्रत्यञ्च् ॥ In strong cases, it is declined as प्रत्यङ्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, प्रत्यञ्चः ॥ प्रत्यञ्चम्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, in weak cases, अ is elided by VI. 4. 138 S. 416, and though this lopa is a bahiraṅga process, while the yaṇ or semivowel Sandhi is an antaraṅga process, yet this lopa is not considered asiddha for the purposes of this sandhi. This proceeds on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. See under Sūtra I. 3. 11 S. 46. Thus Acc: Pl: is प्रतीचः, Instr: Sing is प्रतीचा ॥ &c. प्रति + अञ्च् + शस् = प्रति + च् + अस् ॥ Here two sūtras simultaneously appear for application, viz. इको यणचि and अचः ॥ Now इको यणचि is antaraṅga, because the efficient cause अ of अञ्च् is inside that of शस्; and the efficient cause शस् by which अ of अञ्च् would be elided is outside; therefore yaṇ ādeśa should take place first, thus प्रति + अ + शस् = प्रत्य् + अच् + शस् ॥ After this अ should be elided as प्रत्य् + च् + अस् ॥ This however gives us no form, and so relying on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. the antaraṅga yaṇ substitution is set aside. Now, we take up the declension of अञ्च् as compounded with the pronoun अदस् meaning अमुम् अञ्चति ॥ Thus we have अदस् + अञ्च् + क्विन् । Here applies the following sūtra.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI. DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
418. In the room of the last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, of a Pronoun and of the words विष्वक् and देव, is substituted अद्रि, when अञ्च् has no visible affix following it.
Thus अदस् + अञ्च् = अदद्रि + अञ्च् = अदद्य् + अञ्च्. At this stage, applies the following sūtra.
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI. DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Panini reference digits OCR as 6.3.62 (misread of Devanagari ९ as ६ for 6.3.92).

entries.english:
419. When the pronoun अदस् does not end in स्, then there is substituted उ or ऊ for the vowel after द्, and म् for द् ॥
The short u in the sūtra is a samāhāra dvandva compound including both the short u and long ऊ. By the rule of antartama I. 1. 50 S. 39, the short vowel and the consonant following it will be replaced by the short u; and the long vowel with the consonant following it will be replaced by the long ū.
Thus अदद्य् + अञ्च् = अमुमुद्य् + अञ्च् : the first द् and अ are changed to म् and उ, and the second द् and य् are also changed to म् and उ; so the declension is:—
Nom. Sing. अमुमुयङ् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुयञ्चः
Acc. Sing. अमुमुयञ्चम् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुचः
Ins. Sing. अमुमुचा Dual अमुमुयग्भ्याम् &c. &c.
The mutva being considered as asiddha, there is no sandhi in
entries.chapter: CHAPTER XI. DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Text cut off at the bottom of page 244; table reconstructed from OCR fragments.

entries.english:
in æg, for the Sandhi rule is contained in the Sixth Book of Panini, while this g substitute is ordained in the Tripadi portion of Ashtadhyayi. Hence the Sutra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12 applies.
Some, by applying the following maxim, get the form
Paribhasha "When a modification is ordained with regard to something which is not final, the operation takes place on that only which is in proximity to the final." The second class apply this maxim and make g change only for which stands in proximity to the final.
There is a third form, which is obtained by explaining the असेः in the Sutra as मः सेर्यस्य सोऽयमसिः, तत्र सकारस्य मकारः क्रियते ॥ "The word असेः in the sutra is a Bahuvrihi, and means that in which अस् is substituted for ‹?›" The sutra is thus confined to the form derived by changing the द् into म् by VII. 2. 102. and not to any other.
Thus there are three views with regard to the application of the present sutra:—
(1) the d of adas, and of adri are both changed to m by the present sutra; (2) the first is not changed, but only the second; (3) none is changed. Thus we have (1) अमूमुयङ् (VII. 1. 70, VI. 1. 68, VIII. 2. 23 and 62), अमूमुयञ्चौ, अमूमुयञ्चः ॥ (2) Secondly, अदमुयङ्, अदमुयञ्चौ, अदमुयञ्चः ॥ (3) Lastly अद्रिर्यङ्, अद्रियञ्चौ, अद्रियञ्चः ॥ The above verse summarises this:
Verse:—Some ordain that m should come separately for both adas and adri, as there is double d (in see sutra VIII. 2. 80 and VII. 4. 90 S. 2644); others would have m only for the last portion which stands in proximity to the final, (i.e. for adri); while a third class would have m nowhere, because they explain असेः of the sutra by confining it to Tyadadi VII. 2. 102."
Note:—Thus उदङ् = विष्वक्. This form is thus evolved. अञ्च् + क्विन् = अञ्च् + ० = अञ्च् + नुम् (VII. 1. 70). Then there is elision of the final conjunct consonant, then the final dental is changed to guttural because of the क्विन् affix (VIII. 2. 62), i.e. च् is changed to क् and we have ‹?› which with ङि, gives the above form.
प्राङ्, प्रत्यङ्, उदङ् ॥ प्राची and प्रतीची (VI. 3. 95) have acute on the final irregularly (nipatana) in order to prevent the krit-accent, and when ई is changed into य् the following vowel becomes svarita (VIII. 2. 4).
Observe अश्वाव्री—अश्वमञ्चति, the अ of अञ्च् is elided by VI. 4. 138.
Why 'when an affix follows'? Observe प्राची ॥ The न् is totally elided by VI. 4. 24, feminine ङीप् being added by IV. 1. 6 Vart. The अ is elided by VI. 4. 138, and the final of प्र is lengthened by VI. 3. 138.
Why do we say of क्विन् and अनप्रत्यये? Observe अञ्चनम् ॥
Another reading of the sutra is अनवप्रत्यये (नावप्रत्यये) ॥ It would give the same result, the meaning then being when no affix follows. The word अनप्रत्यये or अनवप्रत्यये indicates by implication that in other places where simply a verb is mentioned, it means a word-form beginning with that verb which ends with some affix. For had अनप्रत्यये not been used, then the rule would have applied not only when anch followed, but when anchana ending in ल्युट् also followed. The maxim धातुग्रहणे तदादिविधिरिष्यते is illustrated in अयस्कृते and अयस्कारः; for VIII. 3. 46 teaches that visarga is changed into स् when कृ follows. There the कृ denotes not only the root कृ but a word derived from कृ, therefore which begins with कृ such as कारः and कृतः ॥ Therefore the rule applies to forms like अयस्कृत् which is followed merely by the verb कृ; as well as to forms like अयस्कृतः ॥
Now we take up the declension of उदञ्च्. It is declined in the Nominative as उदङ् (S), उदञ्चौ (Dual) उदञ्चः (Pl).
Before the weak cases the following rule applies:—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
420. Long ई is substituted for the अ of that (अञ्च्) where the nasal is elided after the word उद्, when the stem is Bha.
As उदीचः, उदीचा, उदग्भ्याम् ॥
Now we take up the declension of सम्यञ्च् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
421. समि is substituted for सम्, before this अञ्च् when no visible affix follows.
Thus सम्यक् सम्यङ्, सम्यञ्चौ, सम्यञ्चः ॥
Ac : Pl: समीचः Instr: Sing समीचा ॥
Now we take up the declension of सह + अञ्च् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies —
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
422. सधि is the substitute of सह, before अञ्च् followed by no visible affix.
Thus सध्यङ्, सध्यञ्चौ, सध्यञ्चः; and सध्रीचः, सध्रीचा ॥ See VI. 3. 138 for long vowel.
Now, we take up the declension of तिर्यञ्च् ॥ In its declension, the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
423. तिर्य is substituted for तिरस् before this अञ्च् when no visible affix follows, provided that the अ of अञ्च् is not elided.
Thus तिर्यङ्, तिर्यञ्चौ, तिर्यञ्चः ॥ Why do we say 'when there is no elision'? Observe तिरश्चा, तिरश्चे ॥ Here अ is elided by VI. 4. 138. The word अलोपे in the sutra is ambiguous. It may mean either (1) "where अ is elided" or (2) "where there is no elision." The latter meaning should be taken however.
Now, we take up the declension of प्र + अञ्च् when अञ्च् means 'to honor'. There are two roots (अञ्चु), both belong to the Bhvadi class, one meaning 'to honor' and the other 'to move'. The declension of 'अञ्चु' meaning 'to move' has already been exhibited above. But when it means 'to honor' its declension is governed by the following rule :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS

entries.english:
424. The nasal of अञ्च् is not elided when the meaning is 'to honor'.
And as the nasal is not elided by VI. 4. 24. S. 415 there is no नुम् augment. Thus:
Singular Dual Plural
Nominative प्राङ् प्राञ्चौ प्राञ्चः
As न् is not elided, so there is no elision of अ also by VI. 4. 138. S. 416. Thus the weak forms are Ac : Pl : प्राञ्चः ॥ Inst : Sing and dual are प्राञ्चा, प्राङ्भ्याम् ॥ Loc. Plural is प्राङ्क्षु or प्राक्षु ॥
Similar is the declension of प्रत्यञ्च् when 'अञ्च्' means 'to honor'. Thus Acc: Plu : is प्रत्यञ्चः and not प्रतीचः ॥ Similarly the Acc : Plural of अदमुयञ्च् is अदमुयञ्चः and not अदमुयीचः ॥
Similarly the Acc plural of उदञ्च् is उदञ्चः and not उदीचः ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Entry text cuts off at the bottom of page 247 and continues on page 248.

entries.english:
Now, we take up the declension of ‹?›. This word, as already mentioned in sûtra III. 2. 59 S. 373 is irregularly formed by adding the affix ‹?› to the root meaning "to curve or make crooked" or "to be or become small". Thus it is declined :—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. ‹?› ‹?› ‹?›

Instr. Dual is ‹?› &c.

Now, we take up the declension of पयोमुच्. In Nom. Sing. the ‹?› is changed to the guttural, by Sutra VIII. 2. 30 S. 378. It is declined as follows:—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. पयोमुक् or पयोमुग् पयोमुचौ पयोमुचः &c.

Now, we take up the declension of ‹?› in the sense of ‹?›. It is thus formed :— सु + ‹?› meaning 'that which cuts well'. The ‹?› being vocalised by VI. 1. 16 S. ‹?›, it becomes सु + वृ + श्च. By VIII. 2. 36 S. 294, the श् is changed to ष्. By VIII. 2. 29 S. 380, the initial ‹?› is elided. Thus we get सु + वृट् and finally to ड् by VIII. 2. 39 S. 84 and VIII. 4. 56 S. 206. Thus its declension is as follows:—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. सुवृट् or सुवृड् ‹?› ‹?›

The Loc. Pl. is सुवृत्सु or सुवृट्सु.

*Note:—This would be true in the view that the original root was व्रश्च्, with a dental त् which becomes ट् by ष्टुना ष्टुः VIII. 4. 40 S. 111. This ष्टुत्व substitution is asiddha for VIII. 2. 29.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in त्.

Now, we take up the declension of महत्. This word is formed by the Unadi affix (Unadi sutra II. 84) which means that the words ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?› are irregularly formed with the affix ‹?› with the force of the present tense and are operated upon as if they were followed by a ‹?› affix. Since महत् is to be treated as if it was formed by the ‹?› affix, therefore, the rule VII. 1. 70 S. 361 would cause the insertion of नुम् and the sutra VI. 4. 10 S. 317 would cause the lengthening of आ. Thus.

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. महान् महान्तौ महान्तः
Voc. हे महन् " "
Acc. महान्तम् " महतः
Instr. महता महद्भ्याम् महद्भिः
&c. &c. &c.

-:0:-

Now we take up the declension of धीमत्. It is formed with the affix मतुप्.

-----

In its declension, the following rule applies :—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN त्
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 424 from page 247; includes transitional lead-in to SK 425 printed before the sutra line.

entries.english:
425. In the Nominative Singular (with the exception of the Vocative Singular) the penultimate vowel is lengthened in a stem ending in अतु, and अस् when the consonant (अस्) does not belong to a root.

The नुम् (न्) is added to the above by VII. 1. 70, after the elongation has taken place, for if added before elongation, the vowel no longer being penultimate, will not be lengthened at all. This is because of the force of this sûtra, which though precedent in the order of enunciation in Panini's Ashtadhyayi, and therefore ought to have been superseded by the subsequent and nitya sutra (VII. 1. 70 S. 361) ordaining नुम्, yet is not so. Thus its declension is

Nominative
Singular धीमान्
Dual धीमन्तौ
Plural धीमन्तः

Vocative
हे धीमन्

Before the weak case terminations, it is declined like महत्.

Note:—अस् :— as सुपयाः, सुयशाः, सुश्रोताः ॥ Why do we say 'not belonging to a dhātu'? Observe पिण्डग्रसः where स् belongs to the root ग्रस् (पिण्डं ग्रसते), so also चर्मवः (चर्म वस्ते) ॥ The अस् having no significance as an affix &c. is also included here, on the strength of the maxim "whenever अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are taught in Grammar denote by I. 1. 72, something that ends with these, there they represent these combination of letters, both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of a meaning". (अनिन्नस्मन्ग्रहणेष्वर्थवताऽप्यनर्थकेन च तदन्तविधिं प्रयोजयन्ति) ॥ The word अतु in the sûtra indicates whatever ends in अतु whether when first enunciated (उपदेश), such as वतु, क्तवतु &c. or which assumes the form अतु in grammatical inflection, such as डवतु, which in upadesa ends in अतु, but becomes अतु in प्रयोग or application. In Vocative singular we have हे गोमन्, हे सुपयः, this rule not applying there.

Even in the case of Denominative roots, the lengthening will take place. The prohibition of अधातु in this sûtra applies to original roots and not to derivative roots from nouns. Thus — "He wishes to have cows." The affix क्यच् is added to गोमत् in forming the derivative root by III. 1. 8. or III. 1. 10. with the force of "wishing" or "behaving." The root is गोमत्य. It is a derivative root, and so it does not fall within the prohibition of this sûtra. Now गोमत्य् + क्विप् = गोमत् (अ is dropped by VI. 4. 48, and य् by VI. 4. 50). "One wishing to have cows." Here ends with अत् (which was part of the original affix मतुप् added to गो) and here we will have lengthening as well as नुम् ॥

The नुम् will be added for the following reason:—
In the sûtra उगिदचां VII. 1. 70. S. 361 the root अञ्चु is taken for the sake of niyama or restriction, that is, the operations dependent upon ugit, when applied to roots, will apply to the root añchu only, and not to any other root having an ugit. Thus in स्रंसु and ध्वंसु there is no ugit operation. Therefore, we could have easily inferred that no other root except अञ्चु would take नुम् under that sutra. The specific mention of अधातुः in that sutra would have become redundant. But the fact, that Panini has mentioned अधातुः in that sutra, indicates that by धातु is meant the original root and not a derivative root.

Thus we have
Singular गोमान्
Dual गोमन्तौ
Plural गोमन्तः
"One who wishes to be possessed of cows."

Now we take up the declension of भवत् not derived from भू, but from भा meaning 'to shine'. (see Unâdi sutra I. 63) with the affix डवतु । Thus भा + डवतु = भवत् (the आ is elided by VI. 4. 143 and I. 4. 18 because the affix has an indicatory ड). It is declined as

Nominative
Singular भवान्
Dual भवन्तौ
Plural भवन्तः &c.

But when it is derived from the root भू with the affix शतृ, as it does not then end with the affix अतु, the penultimate is not lengthened. Thus in this case, the Nominative Singular is भवन्.

Now, we take up the declension of ‹?› formed from the root ‹?› with the affix ‹?›. The root is reduplicated. The reduplication is technically
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN त्
entries.note: Text cuts off mid-sentence at bottom of page 250; panini_ref retains printed digits 8.4.14 (misprint for 6.4.14).

entries.english: called अभ्यस्त as defined below, and because it is अभ्यस्त, it does not get the augment नुम्, for the sûtra after next prohibits it.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN त्
entries.note: Tail continuation from page 250.

entries.english: 426. Where reduplication is treated in the Sixth Book of Panini's Ashtadhyayi, the two which are directed, both are collectively called Abhyasta.
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN त्

entries.english:
427. The Participial-affix शतुँ (अत्-अन्त), does not take the augment नुम् after a reduplicate stem.

Thus, ददत्, ददतः ॥

Note:—This is an exception to VII. 1. 70, and applies of course to sarvanâmasthâna or strong cases. The नुम् is to be read into this sûtra, from VII. 1. 70; for the negation of this sûtra cannot apply to ई taught in the preceding sûtra for ई is never ordained after śatṛ: therefore, though several other operations intervene, yet नुम् is to be read here.

Now, we take up the declension of जक्षत्, formed with the affix शतुँ added to the root जक्ष्. Its declension is governed by the following Sûtra:—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN त्
entries.note: Reconstructed corrupted Devanagari words (शतुँ, नुम्, जक्षत्) from context.

entries.english:
428. So also the six roots, with jakshi itself as the seventh, are called abhyasta.

Note:—The word abhyasta is understood here. The verb jakshi and the six verbs that follow it in the Dhatupatha, in all seven verbs, get this designation. These are जक्ष, जागृ, दरिद्रा, चकास्, शास्, दीधी and वेवी ॥ (Panini has overlooked वेवी and mentions only the first six.) By getting the designation of Abhyasta, the participles derived from these verbs are declined like ददत् ॥

Thus जक्षत् or जक्षद् (N. S.); जक्षतौ (N. Dual); जक्षतः (N. Plural).
Similar is the declension of जागृत्, दरिद्रत्, शासत्, चकासत् ॥ दीधी and वेवी though exhibited in the Dhâtupâṭha as दीधीङ् and वेवीङ् with an indicatory ङ् and therefore, they ought to be आत्मनेपदी by I. 3. 12. S. 2158, yet they are परस्मैपदी because of the Vaidic irregularities. These form their Nominative Singulars as दीध्यत् and वेव्यत्.

Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in त्.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्. Now we take up the declension of गुप् which is formed from the चुरादि root गुप् with the affix क्विप्. The आम् of the चुरादि class is optionally elided by III. 1. 31. S. 2305. It is declined as:

Nom: गुप् or गुब्, गुपौ, गुपः; Instr: Dual गुब्भ्याम् &c.

Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in श.

Now, we take up the declension of तादृश् formed according to the following Sûtra:—
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN त्
entries.note: Corrected OCR misreads of verb roots, noun endings, and declensional forms.

entries.english:
429. The affix कञ् as well as क्विन् comes after the verb दृश् ‘to see’ when it is in combination with त्यद् &c. which precede it, and when it does not signify perception.

Note:—The force of 'च' is that the क्विन् also comes under similar circumstances. त्यद् &c. are pronouns, for a list of which see I. 1. 27. Thus तादृश् ॥
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN श

entries.english:
430. आ is substituted for the final of the Pronouns (I. 1. 27) before these words दृग्, दृश् and the affix वतु ॥

Thus तद् + दृश् + क्विन् (by the present sûtra) = ता + दृक् (the श् is changed to क् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377). This is not perceived (असिद्ध) for the purposes of change by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. Thus we have तादृश् = तादृष् = तादृड् (VIII. 2. 39. S. 84) = तादृग् (VIII. 2. 62. S. 377) = तादृक् (optionally by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206).

Thus Nom. forms are तादृक् or तादृग्, तादृशौ, तादृशः. According to the opinion of Kaiyaṭa and Haradatta &c. the form would be तादृख् but never तादृग्, in the alternative when it is not तादृक्. Because they apply the कुत्व rule as an apavâda to व्रश्च rule and by कुत्व they get ख in the place of श (See Padamanjarî p. 953): and ख will never become ग् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84; because ख obtained by क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः VIII. 2. 62. is asiddha or not perceived by the जश्त्व rule VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. Or we may say that ख is not asiddha for Panini himself has changed ख् into ग् in the word दिगादि (See IV. 4. 54. S. 1429).

Now, we take up the declension of विशू. This is formed by the affix क्विप् added to the root विश् 'to enter'. The श् is changed to ष् by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. which is changed to ड् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. and optionally to ट् by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206.

Thus it is declined as:
Sing.	Dual.	Pl.
Nom.	विट् or विड्	विशौ	विशः
Acc.	विशम्	विशौ	विशः
&c.	&c.

Now, we take up the declension of नश्. In its declension, the following rule applies.

entries.english:
431. The final of नश् at the end of a word is optionally changed to a guttural.

Note:—Here the root नश् has taken क्विन् in denoting 'condition or state'; by considering it as belonging to संपदादि class.

Thus there are four forms in the Nominative Singular namely:—नक् or नग् or नट् or नड् ॥

Nominative Dual and Plural are नशौ, नशः.

Instr: Dual is नग्भ्याम् and नड्भ्याम् &c.

Now, we take up the declension of घृतस्पृश्. Its declension is governed by the following rule:—

DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN श

entries.english: 432. The affix क्विन् comes after the verb स्पृश् 'to touch', when it is in composition with a case-inflected word other than उदक 'water'. Thus घृतं स्पृशति = घृतस्पृश्, Nominative Singular घृतस्पृक् 'he who touches clarified butter,' स्पृश् + क्विन् + सु = स्पृश् + ० + ० (VI. 1. 68) = स्पृक् + ० (VI. 1. 67, and VIII. 2. 62). Nominative Dual and Plural are घृतस्पृशौ, घृतस्पृशः respectively. —:o:— In the sutra, VIII. 2. 62, S. 377 if we take the compound as a Bahuvrihi, meaning a root to which the affix can be added, then the gutturalization will take place, even when the affix is added. Thus the root takes the affix when in compound with another word. But when it is used alone it takes the affix . This will also produce the guttural change, because is a root which is liable to take the affix ‹?›. Thus ‹?› &c. Here the ‹?› is changed to ‹?› then to ‹?›, then to ‹?› and then optionally to ‹?› as shown above. Here ends the declension of Nouns ending in श्. Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ष्. Now, we take up the declension of ‹?›. It is formed from the root धृष् 'to be impudent'. Thus धृष् + क्विन् = दधृष् ॥ Here there is reduplication and the final has acute accent. (III. 2. 59. S. 373). The ष् of दधृष् should be ‹?› before gutturalisation. Then this ‹?› must be changed to ‹?› gutturalised to ग् and then is optionally changed to क्. Thus दधृक् or दधृग्, दधृषौ, दधृषः ॥ &c. Now, we take up the declension of रत्नमुष् meaning 'one who steals gems'. It is regularly declined as Sing. Dual. Pl. Nom. रत्नमुट् or रत्नमुड् रत्नमुषौ रत्नमुषः Now, we take up the declension of षष्. It is always plural. By Sutra VII. 1. 22. S. 261, the Nom. and Acc. Pl. terminations are elided after it. Thus Nom. Acc. Pl. are षट् or षड् ॥ Instr. Pl. षड्भिः ॥ Dat. and Abl. Pl. षड्भ्यः ॥ In forming the Genitive Pl. the augment नुट् is added by VII. 1. 55. S. 338. to the case-termination. Thus षष् + नुट् + आम् = षष् + नाम्. By the exception made in the Sutra VIII. 4. 42. S. 114 the न् of नाम् is changed to ण्. Thus षट् + नाम् = षट् + णाम् ॥ The optional substitution of a nasal in the place of ‹?› required by VIII. 4. 45 S. 116 is superseded

by the Vārtika under the same sutra, which requires the nasal substitution compulsorily in the Secular literature. Thus षड् + णाम् = पण्णाम्. The Loc. Pl. is षट्त्सु or षट्सु.

The declension of षष् is the same when it is the final member of a compound. Thus परमषट् (N. Pl.) परमषण्णाम् (G. Pl.). But when it is the secondary member of a compound, the Nom. and G. Pl. are प्रियषषः and प्रियषषाम् respectively.

Here ends the declension of Nouns ending in ष.

entries.english:
Declension of Masculines ending in स्.

We take up the declension of पिपठिस् (meaning 'wishing to read'). It is derived from the root पिपठिस् with the affix क्विप्. The अ of स is elided by VI. 4. 48. S. 2308. The स् was changed to ष् by VIII. 3. 39. S. 153. But this is not perceived by the Sūtra requiring the substitution of स् into रुँ for it is precedent in the order of enumeration in Pāṇini's Ashṭādhyāyī, (VIII. 2. 66. S. 162). Thus पिपठिष् + सु = पिपठिष् + ० (by VI. 1. 68. S. 252). Now पिपठिष् gets the name of a pada though the affix सु is elided after it (I. 1. 62. S. 262). Therefore the ष् which is really स् becomes रुँ. Thus पिपठिष् becomes पिपठिर्. At this stage applies the following Sūtra.

433. A penultimate ik is lengthened, when the final r or v of a root can stand at the end of a Pada.
Thus पिपठिर् becomes पिपठीः.
The Nominative Dual and Plural are पिपठिषौ and पिपठिषः.
The Inst: Dual is पिपठीर्भ्याम्.
In forming the Locative Plural the sūtra VIII. 3. 36 S. 151 as well as the following comes into operation.

entries.english:
434. The substitution of ष for स takes place then also, when any one of these singly, namely, the augment नुम् (or anusvāra), the visarjanîya or a sibilant occurs between the said इण् and कु letters or the affix.

Thus पिपठीस् + सुप् = पिपठीस् (the इ of पिपठीस् is lengthened by the last sutra, because the base before this affix gets the designation of pada by I. 4. 17. S. 230) + सु = (the स being changed to ष by the present sutra) पिपठीःषु or पिपठीः षु ॥

The ष takes place, when नुम् &c. intervene singly and not when they intervene collectively. Therefore not here सुपिन्त्स, 'thou kissest', 'kiss thou', from the root ‹?› 'to kiss'. Here there is the intervention of two, namely, नुम् and स (III. 4. 91).

From the explanation in Mahâbhâshya in explaining ‹?› we learn that the anusvāra of this sûtra must be the anusvâra which replaces नुम् and not any other anusvâra. Therefore not here. Here there is no change.

Though anusvâra was included in the pratyâhâra शर by the Vârtika—"the visarjanîya, anusvâra, jihvâmûlîya and upadhmânîya should be included in the pratyâhâra शर for the sake of ‹?› vidhi and ‹?› vidhi"; yet the separate mention in this sûtra indicates that that anusvâra is to be taken which results from नुम्.

Now, we take up the declension of चिकीर्ष् : This is formed from the Desiderative root कृ meaning 'wishing to make' with the affix क्विप्. This is thus formed :— कृ + सन् ॥ Here the augment इट् is not added because of the sutra VII. 2. 10. S. 2246 or VII. 2. 12. S. 2610; the affix सन् is ‹?› by I. 2. 9. S. 2612 and therefore there is no guna by I. 1. 5. S. 2217. Then there is lengthening of the vowel by VI. 4. 16. S. 2614. Then the ऋ is changed to ईर् by VII. 1. 100. S. 299. Then the root is reduplicated by VI. 1. 9. S. 2395.

Thus we get चिकीर् + स. The first क is elided by VII. 4. 60. S. 2179 and first changed to च by VII. 4. 62. S. 2245. Thus we have चिकीर्स. Now, चिकीर्स + क्विप् — चिकीर्स् ॥ Then the अ of सन् is elided by VI. 4. 48 S. 2308.

To this is added the N. S. case termination सु ॥ चिकीर्स् + सु ॥ The affix सु is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. Now the final स् is elided by VIII. 2. 24. S. 280. Thus we have चिकिर् ॥ The इ of चिकिर् is lengthened by VIII. 2. 76 S. 433.

entries.english:
The lengthening in ‹?› &c. is by VI. 4. 16. S. 2614 by which the ‹?› is lengthened before ‹?› affix. We did not apply this sûtra, in Nominative S. because ‹?› was already dropped.
Thus the Nominative forms are ‹?› || The lengthening takes place by VIII. 2. 76, 77. S. 433. and 354.
The Loc: Plural is ‹?›. Here ‹?› is not changed to visarga, because it is not the ‹?› of ‹?› but it is a portion of the word itself (see sûtra VIII. 3. 16. S. 339.)
Now, we take up the declension of ‹?›: This is formed by the Uṇâdi affix ‹?› added to the root ‹?› (Uṇâdi II. 69). The ‹?› of ‹?› is elided because the affix after it has an indicatory ‹?› see VI. 4. 143 S. 316, though the base is not ‹?›. Thus ‹?›. Then ‹?› is changed to ‹?›. But this change is asiddha for the purposes of ‹?› and visarga change. Thus N. S. is ‹?› : N. Dual and Plural are ‹?›, respectively. In the weak cases it has two forms, thus, ‹?› or दोषः (Ac. Plural); दोषणा or दोषा (Inst: singular), for in these cases ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› by VI. 1. 63. S. 228.
Note:—The portion of ‹?› is elided by VI. 4. 143. S. 316, and though the base before it is not strictly speaking ‹?› Sûtra VI. 4. 143 could not apply here, for that sûtra is confined to ‹?› bases only. But as the ‹?› of the affix ‹?› must produce some effect, it produces the elision of ‹?› portion of ‹?› by the analogy of VI. 4. 143.
Now, we take up the declension of ‹?›: It is formed from the root विश् with the Desiderative affix सन् ॥ Thus विश् + सन् ॥ The augment ‹?› is not added because of the prohibition contained in VII. 2. 10. S. 2246. The affix is कित् by I. 2. 12. S. 2368 and therefore there is no guṇa. Thus विश् + सन् = विविश् + स ॥ To this we add the affix क्विप् by which the अ of स is elided by VI. 4. 48. अतो लोपः and we get the form विविश्स् ॥ Then by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54. ‹?› is elided and we get ‹?› ॥ This is changed to ‹?› by VIII. 2. 36 S. 294 which again is changed to ‹?› and then optionally to ‹?› by VIII. 2. 41. S. 295; and ‹?› changed to ‹?› by VIII. 3. 57 S. 211. Thus N. forms are विविट् or विविद्, विविक्षौ, विविक्षः ॥
Now we take up the declension of ‹?› formed from the root तक्ष् or त्वक्ष् 'to fashion'. The ‹?› is elided by VIII. 2. 29. S. 380. Thus the N. S. is तद् or तङ् formed under the same rules as विविद् or विविट्.
Nominative Dual and Plural are तक्षौ तक्षः.
Similar is the declension of ‹?› meaning 'one who protects cows'. Its N. forms are गोरद् or गोरड्, गोरक्षौ गोरक्षः ॥
But if these words be derived from the Causative roots (ण्यन्त) तक्षि and ‹?› with the affix ‹?›, then VIII. 2. 29. S. 380 will not apply and so there will be no elision of ‹?›. This is because the णि which was elided by णेरनिटि (VI. 4. 51. S. 2313) will be स्थानिवत् ॥ But will not the following Vârtika पूर्वत्रासिद्धीयॆ न स्थानिवत् prevent the स्थानिवद्भाव ? 'There is no sthânivadbhâva in the last three chapters of Ashṭâdhyâyî.'
To this we reply 'No'. Because of the following exception. Vârtika:—The above Vârtika is inapplicable in the following three cases (a) the rule ordaining the elision of the first or initial letter of a conjunct consonant VIII. 2. 29. S. 380, (b) the rule relating to ‹?› change (c) the rule relating to ‹?› change. S. 235.
Therefore, we shall have ‹?› i.e. the elision of the final and not of the initial ‹?›. Thus the N. S. will be तक् or तग्; गोरक् or गोरग्.
Now we take up the declension of ‹?› meaning 'desirous of cooking'. It is formed from the root ‹?› with the Desiderative affix ‹?›. Thus we get ‹?› ॥ The अ of the initial प is changed to इ by VII. 4. 79. S. 2317. Thus we have ‹?› ॥ Its N. S. is विपक् or पिपत् ॥ The क् of पिपक्ष is not elided, but the final ‹?› is elided, for the reasons already given above.
Similar is the declension of ‹?› meaning 'desirous of speech' from the root ‹?› 'to speak' and of ‹?›, meaning 'desirous of burning', from the root दह 'to burn'. The Nominative Singular being ‹?› and ‹?› respectively.
Now, we take up the declension of सुपिस् : It is derived from the root ‹?› 'to walk'; hence means 'one who walks well'. It is declined as follows:—
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nominative ‹?› ‹?› ‹?›
Instr. सुपिसा
Loc. सुपिसु or सुपिःसु ॥
Similar is the declension of ‹?› 'well-cutting'. Its Nominative Sing. is ‹?› ॥
Now, we take up the declension of विद्वस् meaning 'a learned man'.
In the strong case terminations, it is declined as :—
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nominative विद्वान् विद्वांसौ विद्वांसः
Voc. हे विद्वन् विद्वांसौ
Acc. विद्वांसम्
In the weak-case terminations, the declension of this word is governed by the following rule :—

entries.english:
435. The semi-vowel of the affix वस् (क्वसु) is vocalised to उ in a Bha stem.
Thus विद् + शस् = विद् + उस् + शस् ॥ and ‹?› become ‹?› by the पूर्वरूप rule (VI. 1. 108 S. 330) = विदुस् + अस् ॥ Then स् of विदुस् is changed to ष् ॥ Thus विदुष् + अस् = विदुषस् = विदुषः (Ac: Pl:), The Ins. Sing: विदुषा is also similarly formed.
Before भ्याम्, the स् of विद्वस् is changed to द् by VIII. 2. 72. S. 334. Thus विद्वद्भ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of सेदिवस् । It is formed by adding the affix क्वसु to the root सद् by III. 2. 108 S. 3097. The root is reduplicated by VI. 1. 8. S. 2177. Thus :— सद् + सद् + वस् ॥ The first द् being elided by हलादि शेषः VII. 4. 60. S. 2179. Then the first स is elided and the अ of the second स is changed into ए by अत एकहल्मध्ये VI. 4. 120. S. 2260. Thus we get सेद् + वस् = सेदिवस् ॥ To this we apply the augment इट् by VII. 2. 67. S. 3096. Thus सेद् + इ + वस् = सेदिवस् ॥ In strong cases there will be नुम् augment by VII. 1. 70. S. 361, and lengthening by VI. 4. 10 S. 317. Thus :—
Singular, Dual, Plural.
Nominative सेदिवान् सेदिवांसौ सेदिवांसः
Acc. सेदिवसम् सेदिवांसौ
In the weak-case terminations or Bha bases, there is not the इट् augment of VII. 2. 67. S. 3096, though it was antaranga, because it would be useless to add इट् when we are going to vocalise the व् into उ for then the efficient cause व् of वस् would be absent. This proceeds on the maxim अकृतव्यूहा &c. See under Sûtra I. 3. 11. S. 46. Because इट् is added to वस् only when it has the form of वस्. But when व् is going to be changed to उ and the affix ultimately becomes उस् then there would be no वस् for the application of the sûtra VII. 2. 67. So we have the Acc: Pl सेदुषः ॥ The Instr: Sing is सेदुषा ॥ The Instr: Dual is सेदिवद्भ्याम् &c.
In the sûtra VI. 4. 10 S. 317, the words ending in conjunct consonant न्स् must be pratipadikas, that is, the crude nouns and not a verbal base ending in न्स्. This we infer because of the pratipadika महत् being in
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN स्
entries.note: Head fragment cut off at the bottom of page 259.

entries.english:
the company of सान्त, which means that words sui generis with महत् should be taken.
Therefore the word सुहिन्स् where the न्स् is a portion of the verb हिनस्ति and where the noun सुहिन्स् means one who strikes well, the rule above given will not apply. Thus सुहिन्स् is declined as follows :--
Nominative Singular. सुहिन् Dual. सुहिन्सौ Plural. सुहिन्सः
In the Instru : Dual where सुहिन्स् gets the designation of pada, the स् is elided and we get सुहिन्भ्याम् ॥
The Loc : Plural is सुहिन्त्सु or सुहिन्सु ॥
Now, we take up the declension of ध्वस् formed from the root ध्वन्स् with the affix क्विप्. The न् of the root ध्वन्स् is elided by VI. 4. 24. S. 415. Thus it is declined as
Singular. ध्वस् or ध्वद् Dual. ध्वसौ Plural. ध्वसः ॥
Instr: Dual. ध्वद्भ्याम् ॥
Similar is the declension of स्त्रस् from the root स्त्रंस् .
Now we take up the declension of पुंस्: In its declension, the following rule applies :--
entries.chapter: DECLENSION OF MASCULINE NOUNS ENDING IN CONSONANTS
entries.note: Tail fragment continuing from preceding page; some Devanagari reconstructed from context.

entries.english:
436. असुङ् ( अस् ) is substituted for the final of पुंस् when the sarvanāmasthāna affixes are to be added.
The उ in असुङ् is for the sake of pronunciation and not to indicate that नुम् should be added under VII. 1. 70 S. 361 because the नुम् will be added in strong cases by the very fact that the word पुंस् is formed from पा ( to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178 ) and as the affix डुम्सुन् is an उगित् affix, it will produce its effect under VII. 1. 70 by causing नुम् pari passu as it does in causing ङीप् to be added to in the feminine, in forming बहुपुंसी, by the sūtra उगितश्च ( IV. 1. 6 S. 455 ) Thus it is declined as follows:--
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. पुमान् पुमांसौ पुमांसः
Voc. हे पुमन्
Acc. पुंसः
Inst. पुंसा पुंभ्याम् पुम्भिः
Loc. पुंसु
Kāśikā:--
The word is derived from पा (to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178), the न् being changed to anusvāra. So when ‹?› of पुंस् is replaced by असुङ् we get the form पुमस्, the उ of असुङ् indicates that नुम् should be added in the strong cases after म ( VII. 1. 70 ), so we have पुमान्, पुमांसौ, पुमांसः ॥
This substitution must take place in its incipient stage before the affixes are added, (अङ्गस्य) : otherwise the accent will be wrong. The compounds have acute on the final, (VI. 1. 223 ), therefore, परमपुंस् has acute on पुं, and in the Nominative Singular the acute will remain on पु, but it is intended that it should be on मा, thus परमपुमान् ॥ The simple word पुंस्, of course, has accent on पु.
Now, we take up the declension of उशनस्. By VII. 1. 94. S. 276, अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Nom. Sing: Thus Nom. forms are उशना, उशनसौ, उशनसः ॥
In forming the Voc: Sing: the following Vārtika will apply :—
Vārt :— अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Voc. S. also, as an alternative, the final न् not being elided (See VIII. 2. 8). Otherwise we have three forms in the Vocative Singular: as हे उशनन्, हे उशन, and हे उशनः ॥
The Instr Dual is उशनोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of अनेहस् meaning 'time'.
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. अनेहा अनेहसौ अनेहसः
Voc. हे अनेहः
Instr. अनेहोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of वेधस् meaning 'the Creator'.
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. वेधाः वेधसौ वेधसः
Voc. हे वेधः
Instr. वेधोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of सुवस् meaning 'one who wears well'. Here वस् belongs to a root and so in the Nom: S. its vowel is not lengthened because of the prohibition of अधातु in VI. 4. 14. S. 425.
Hence its Nom forms are सुवः, सुवसौ, सुवसः ॥
Now we take up the declension of पिण्डग्रस् and पिण्डग्रसस् ॥ The verbs ग्रस् and ग्रसु mean 'to swallow'; the Nominative singular forms of these are पिण्डग्रः and पिण्डग्रसः meaning 'a lump eater'.
Now, we take up the declension of अदस्. In its declension the following rules apply :--

entries.english:
437. For the ‹?› of अदस् there is substituted औ whereby the Nominative affix सु is elided.
As अदस् + सु = अद + औ + 0 ( VII. 2. 107 ) = अस + औ ( VII. 2. 106 S. 381 ) = असौ ॥
Vārt:— When the augment अकच् is added, the औ substitution is optional, and in that alternative उत्व is added after स; as असुकः or असकौ ॥
The form असुकः is thus evolved :-- असकस् + सु, now औ substitution of the present sūtra is prohibited; therefore, the substitution of VII. 2. 102 takes place, and the द् is changed to स by VII. 2. 106, and the अ of अकच् after स is changed to उ.
In forming अमू we observe the following process :--
अदस् + औ = अद + औ ( VII. 2. 102. S. 265. and VI. 1. 97. S. 191 ) = अमू ॥
Here द् is replaced by म् and औ by ऊ; one might object that by the maxim (19) भाव्यमानेन सवर्णानां ग्रहणं न i. e. “A letter which is taught in a rule does not denote the letters homogeneous with it” औ ought to have been changed to short उ, but we answer that the maxim (20) भाव्यमानोऽप्युकारः सवर्णान् गृह्णाति “The letter उ denotes, even when it is taught in a rule, also the letters homogeneous with it,” makes an exception in the case of उ only.
The rule of VIII. 2. 80, (VIII. 2. 1. S. 12) should be applied before the operations required by vibhakti take place, and then the म् and ऊ should be substituted: because with regard to (VII. 2. 102 S. 265) which is a rule of the 7th Adhyāya, the sūtra (VIII. 2. 80. S. 419) which is a rule of Tripādī becomes asiddha. Therefore if the vibhakti operation ordained by VII. 2. 102 S. 265 were not to take place first, then the base would remain a ending with द्, and the rule VIII. 2. 80. S. 419 requiring म् for द्, and ऊ for औ would find no scope at all.

entries.english: But if in the sûtra, the operations of Tripâdî themselves were intended to become asiddha, then we could never get the forms ‹?› &c. For if we apply VIII. 2. 80 S. 419. before the ‹?› of ‹?› obtained by VII. 2. 102 S. 265. plus the ‹?› of the ‹?› become ‹?› by VI. 1. 97 S 191; in other words, if we apply VIII. 2. 80 S. 419 to the following nascent state of ‹?›, then we shall have this incongruity: ‹?›. Here ‹?› is asiddha for the purposes of VI. 1. 97. S. 191, and ‹?› plus ‹?› would become ‹?›, which is not desired. In forming the N. Dual, the rule VII. 2. 102. S. 265 will cause the replacement of ‹?› by ‹?› and this will coalesce with the final ‹?› of ‹?› and become ‹?› by VI. 1. 97 and thus the base will be ‹?›. Thus ‹?›. The ‹?› will be replaced by ‹?› and ‹?› by long ‹?› and we get ‹?› (VII. 2. 102. S. 164). The N. Pl. is ‹?›. It is thus evolved :— ‹?› (VIII. 2. 17 S. 214) ‹?› + ई (VI. 1. 87. S. 69). Then applies the following Sûtra :—

entries.english: 438. For the ‹?› coming after the ‹?› of अदस् there is substituted दू, and ‹?› is changed to ‹?›, when plurality is to be expressed. Thus Nom. Pl. is अमी. In forming the Acc. Sing. we have ‹?› + ‹?›. Now the sûtra ‹?› (VII. 2. 102 S. 265) has superior force to sûtra ‹?› (VIII. 2. 80. S. 419) and it applies first. Thus we get ‹?› + ‹?› = ‹?› because vibhakti operations are applied first. Then applies the sûtra ‹?› (VIII. 2. 80.) and we get अमुम्. When ‹?› is changed to ‹?› it gets the designation of घि (I. 4. 7 S. 232). So in the Inst. Sing. the substitute ना offers itself from VII. 3. 120 S. 244. Thus ‹?›. Here however the question might occur that the formation of ‹?› being enunciated in VIII. 2. 80. S. 419 in the Tripâdî, whether VII. 3. 120 S. 244 does not regard the ‹?› as asiddha. Hence the following Sûtra :—

entries.english: 439. The sûtra VIII. 2. 80, teaching the substitution of ‹?› for the ‹?› of the Pronoun, is however not treated as asiddha in relation to the case-ending ना. Note:— The existence of ‹?› is not considered uneffected when there is to be added ‹?›. On the contrary it is considered as siddha or existing: Thus being considered as siddha, ‹?› gets the designation of ghi by I. 4. 7. and as such, its Instrumental Singular is by VII. 3. 120. अमुना || Had the ‹?› been considered as non-effected, then the stem would not have been called ghi, and there would have been no ‹?› added. But when ‹?› had been added, then the ‹?› being asiddha, ‹?› is considered to be as ending in ‹?›, and this would require lengthening by ‹?› VII. 3. 102: but it is not done on the maxim सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य 'that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination'. There being no lengthening the ‹?› of ‹?› remains short. Or this sûtra may be considered to be the condensation of two sûtras (1) ‹?› is siddha when ‹?› is to be added, (2) is siddha when any operations, otherwise to be caused when ‹?› is added, are to take place. Or the sense of the sûtra is ‹?› परतो यत् प्राप्नोति तस्मिन् कर्त्तव्ये मुभावो नासिद्धः 'the ‹?› is not non-effected in relation to any operation that would otherwise be occasioned when followed by ‹?›'. From this, it would follow by implication that ‹?› must be considered valid for the purposes of ‹?› itself. So being always siddha, ‹?› is added: and there is no lengthening. Thus the declension of अदस् in the Instr. and the succeeding cases is as follows:— Sing. Dual. Plural. Instr. अमुना अमूभ्याम् अमीभिः Dat. अमुष्मै अमूभ्याम् अमीभ्यः Abl. अमुष्मात् अमूभ्याम् अमीभ्यः Gen. अमुष्य अमुयोः अमीषाम् Loc. अमुष्मिन् अमुयोः अमीषु Here end the declensions of Masculines ending in consonants.

entries.english: Now we take up the declension of Feminines ending in ‹?› such as उपानह् ॥ The following rule applies to it. 440. The ‹?› of नह् is changed to ध् before a jhal letter or at the end of a word. Note:— As ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, उपानत् परीणत् ॥ The त् of the affixes क्त &c. is changed to ध् by VIII. 2. 40; and for the preceding ‹?› is substituted ‹?› by VIII. 4. 53. ‹?› is formed by VIII. 2. ‹?›, read with VIII. 4. ‹?›. परीणत् is formed by क्विप् as it belongs to सम्पदादि class, the lengthening is by VI. 3. 116, and ‹?› change by VIII. 4. 14. It would have shortened the processes of transformation, had only ‹?› been ordained in the sûtra, instead of ध्; but the ordaining of ध् is for the purposes of VIII. 2. 40, by which there should be ‹?› for the participial त् &c. in ‹?›, and that there should not be the change of this Nishtha into न् by VIII. 2. 42. Thus नध् + त = नध् + ध (VIII. 2. 40) = नद्ध (VIII. 4. 53). But had the substitute been द्, we should have नद् + त = ‹?› by VIII. 2. 42. Thus उपानह् becomes उपानत् or उपानद् ॥ The Nom. S. affix is elided by VI. 1. 67. and VI. 1. 68, and ध् is changed to त् or द् by VIII. 2. 39. The Nom. D. is उपानहौ and the Plural उपानहः ॥ The Instrumental Dual उपानद्भ्याम् and the Loc. Plural उपानत्सु. Now we take up the declension of the word उष्णिह्. This word is formed with the upasarga उत् and the affix क्विन् by III. 2. 59 added to the root स्निह् 'to love'. The word उष्णिह् is the name of a Vaidic metre. The त् of उत् is elided by nipâtana, the स् and न् are changed to ष् and ण् (VIII. 3. 59. and VIII. 4. 40). The ह is changed to घ because it is a word formed with the affix क्विन् by sûtra VIII. 2. 62. The घ् becomes ग् then by VIII. 2. 39. Thus we have Nom. S. उष्णिक् or उष्णिग्, Nom. D. उष्णिहौ, Nom. Pl. उष्णिहः, Ins. D. उष्णिग्भ्याम्, Loc. Pl. उष्णिक्षु.

Now we take up the declension of words ending in व् such as दिव्.
Here the same rules will apply as in the case of the Masculine word दिव्.
See Sûtra VII. 1. 84. S. 336 &c. Nom. S. द्यौः Nom. D. दिवौ Nom. Pl.
दिवः Loc. Plu. द्युषु.

—:0:—

Now we take up the declension of words ending in र् such as गिर्. It
is declined as the masculine word. Thus Nom. S. गीः, D. गिरौ, Pl. गिरः.
Similar is the declension of पुर्. The word चतुर् is changed to चतसृ. It is
always declined in the Plural. Thus Nom. and Acc. Pl. चतस्रः, Gen. Pl.
चतसृणाम् ॥

—:0:—

Now we take up the declension of words ending in म् such as किम्.
क is substituted for किम् by VII. 2. 103. Then we add the feminine affix टाप्.
Thus Nom. S. is का Nom. D. के Nom. Pl. काः. The declension of the rest is
like the feminine form of सर्व (सर्वा).

—:0:—

Now, we take up the declension of इदम्. Its declension is governed
by the following rule :—

entries.english:
441. य is substituted for the द् of इदम् in the Nominative Singular in the feminine.

The final मू of इदम् remains unchanged by VII. 2. 108. S. 343. Thus Nominative S. इयम् ॥ Then the feminine affix टाप् is added by the sûtra VII. 2. 102. S. 265. ‹?› is changed to ‹?› by VII. 2. 109. S. 345. The Nominative Dual is इमे Nominative Plural इमाः ॥ Accusative S. is इमाम् Inst. S. is अनया ॥ ‹?› is changed to अन् by VII. 2. 112. By the rule VII. 2. 113. S. 347 there is elision of ‹?› so that we have in the Inst. Dat. and Abl. Dual आभ्याम् ; Inst. Plural is आभिः. We have Dat. S. अस्यै by VII. 3. 114 ; Gen. S. अस्याः and Dual अनयोः by VII. 3. 105 and Plural आसाम् by VII. 1. 52 and VII. 2. 113 ; Loc. S. अस्याम्, D. अनयोः, and Plural आसु ॥ But in re-employment (अन्वादेश) we have एनाम् in the Acc. S. एने in the Dual and एनाः in Plural. In Inst. S. एनया, and एनयोः in the Dual of both Genitive and Locative.

Now we take up the declension of words ending in ज् such as स्रज्.
The word स्रज् is formed by the sûtra III. 2. 59. with the augment अम् irregularly. Thus we have स्रक् or स्रग् in the Nominative S., स्रजौ in the Dual and स्रजः in the Plural ; स्रग्भ्याम् in the Inst. Dual, स्रक्षु in the Loc. Plural.

Now we take up the declension of words ending in द्, such as त्यद् :—
By the rule VII. 2. 102 and with the feminine affix टाप् we have त्या in the Nominative S., त्ये in the Nom. D., and त्याः in the Nominative Plural. तद्, यद् and एतद् are similarly declined.

Now we take up the declension of words ending in च् e. g. वाच् : We have वाक् or वाग् in the Nominative S., वाचौ in D. and वाचः in the Nominative Plural. In the Instru. D. we have वाग्भ्याम् and in the Loc. Plural वाक्षु ॥

Now we take up the declension of words ending in प् such as अप्. अप् is always used in the Plural. By VI. 4. 11. S. 277. the vowel अ is lengthened. Thus we have in the Nominative Plural आपः ; in the Acc. Plural अपः ॥

In forming the Inst. Plural the following rule applies :—

442. त् is substituted for the final of the stem अप् before a case-ending beginning with भ् ॥

Thus we have अद्भिः and in the Dat. and Abl. Plural अद्भ्यः in the Gen. and Loc. Plural अपाम् and अप्सु respectively.

Now we come to the declension of words ending in श् such as दिश् ॥ Thus in the Nominative S. we have दिक् or दिग् by III. 2. 59. S. 373 and VIII. 2. 62 S. 377 ; in the Nominative Dual दिशौ and Plural दिशः ; in the Inst. Dual दिग्भ्याम् and Loc. Plural दिक्षु ॥

Now we take up the declension of the word दृश् ॥ By the rule III. 2. 60. S. 429 दृश् takes the affix क्विन् when in combination with the pronoun त्यद् &c. But we infer from this that the root दृश् will take the affix क्विन् even when it is not in combination also. Thus in the Nominative S. we have दृक् or दृग् Nominative D. दृशौ, Plural दृशः ॥

So also त्विष् : Its Nominative S. is त्विट् or त्विड् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84., in the Nominative D. ‹?›, Nominative Plural ‹?›, Inst. D. त्विड्भ्याम् and the Loc. Plural त्वित्सु or त्विट्त्सु with the optional augment ‹?› by VIII. 3. 29. S. 131.

The word सजुष्, "a friend". By the rule VIII. 2. 66. S. 162, रु is substituted for its final and by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54. there is the elision of उ ; then by applying the rules VIII. 2. 76. S. 433. and VIII. 3. 15. S. 76. we have ‹?› in the Nominative S. The Nominative D. ‹?› and Plural सजुषः ; similarly in the Inst. D. ‹?› and Loc. Plural सजुष्षु or सजूःषु, the change of ‹?› to ‹?› caused by VIII. 4. 41. S. 113 being not perceived by VIII. 2. 66. S. 162, causing र् ॥

In the same way the word आशिस् is declined. Thus we have आशीः, आशिषौ and आशिषः respectively ; the Nominative S., D. and Plural ‹?› and ‹?› ; In Inst. D. we have आशीर्भ्याम् and Plural आशीर्भिः ॥

Now we take up the declension of the pronoun अदस् :

Nom. असौ (VII. 2. 102. S. 265) अमू (VIII. 2. 80. S. 419) अमूः
Acc. अमूम् अमू अमूः
Inst. अमुया अमूभ्याम् अमूभिः
Dat. अमुष्यै (VII. 3. 114. S. 291) अमूभ्याम् अमूभ्यः
Abl. अमुष्याः अमूभ्याम् अमूभ्यः

Loc. अमुष्याम् अमुयोः अमूषु

entries.english:
CHAPTER XIII.

DECLENSION OF NEUTERS ENDING IN CONSONANTS.

We take up the declension of the word स्वनडुह्. By the rule VII. 1. 23 S. 319 we have the elision of the case endings सु and अम्. In the case of स्वनडुह् by the application of the rule VIII. 2. 72. S. 334. द् is substituted for ह्. Thus we get स्वनडत् or स्वनडुद् in the Nominative Sing. स्वनडुही in the Nominative Dual by the rule VII. 1. 19. S. 310. In the Nominative Plural, by the rule VII. 1. 98, S. 331, we have the augment आम् ॥ Thus we get स्वनड्वांहि. The Accusative forms will be the same as the Nominative. The rest is declined like the Masculine.

Now we take up the declension of the words ending in दिव् such as विमलदिव् ॥ By the rule VI. 1. 131, S. 337, उ is substituted for the final व् : thus we get विमलद्यु in the Nominative Singular which means "a clear day".

In forming the Dual, there arises this consideration :—the word विमलदिव् is a compound of two words विमल and दिव् ॥ When the compounds are formed, the case affixes are elided, as राज्ञः पुरुषः = राजपुरुषः. But though the case-affix is elided, the first member retains the designation of Pada, and so the न् of राजन् is elided and the form is rāja-purusha and not rājan-purusha. Similarly in वागीशः the क् is changed to ग् ॥ Now if this elided case affix (antarvartinī vibhakti) is efficient in the case of the first member of a compound, analogically should not the second member of the compound get the designation of Pada, for the affix is elided after the second member also, just as the first member gets ? This doubt is removed by the following vārtika.

Vārtika :—The rule of "Pratyaya-lope pratyaya lakshaṇam" does not hold good in the case of the second member of a compound, for the purposes of applying any rule other than that relating to the initial letter of a Pada". Therefore, there is no pratyaya-lakshaṇa: and so the word दिव् in विमलदिव् does not get the designation of pada and so it gets the designation Bha; and consequently we can apply to it the sūtra VII. 1. 19 S. 310, which applies to Bha bases only. विमलदिव् being a Bha base and not a Pada, the औ is changed to शी ; and we get the Nominative Dual विमलदिवी and not विमलद्यौः ॥ The Nominative Plural is विमलदीवि.

Why do we say in the above vārtika अपदादिविधौ "when any rule not relating to the beginning of a Pada is to be applied" ? Observe दधिसेचौ a Genitive Tatpurusha, compounded from दध्नः + सेचौ = दधिसेचौ. Here the second term does get the designation of Pada for the purposes of the application of the rule which prevents the initial स् being changed to ष्. Had it not been a Pada then स् would have been changed to ष् after दधि by VIII. 3. 58. S. 434. But though it is treated as a Pada for the purposes of the application of the preventive rule relating to the initial letter, yet it is not to be treated as Pada for the purposes of the application of the rule to the final letter च् which would become guttural if it were a Pada.

Note :—सेच् is derived from the root सिच् ‘to sprinkle;’ with the affix क्विप् (III. 2. 75. S. 2980). The above is the illustration of Genitive Tatpurusha compound.

Obj:—But if we form the upapada compound with the root सिच् and the upapada दधि in the Accusative, as दधि सिञ्चतः, then since the compounding is ordained to take place before the addition of vibhaktis, the word has no pada designation, and so does not begin a pada, and it should be changed to ष्. Thus in upapada-samāsa, the change is inevitable.

Ans :—To this Kaiyaṭa replies “अनभिधानात् सोपपदात् क्विब्भावः, दधिषेचौ इति प्रयोगाभावात् ” ॥ Or we may say that the word अपदादि means पदात् परस्यादिः the beginning of a subsequent (whether pada or not) preceded by a pada.

Now, we take up the declension of वार्. Its N. S. and Dual are वार् and वारी respectively. In forming the N. Pl. there will be no नुम् ordained by VII. 1. 72: S. 314, because the base does not end in झल् letters. Therefore the N. Pl. is वारि.

The Nominative and Acc. Pl. of चतुर् is चत्वारि ॥ The rest is like the masculine.

Now we take up the declension of किम्. Thus किम् + सु = किम् + ० by VII. 1. 23. S. 319. Now the affix is elided by using the word लुक् and so it leaves no trace behind, by I. 1. 63. S. 263, and therefore किम् is not changed to कम् as would otherwise be required by Sūtra VII. 2. 103. S. 342. Thus it is declined as :—

Nom. Sing. किम्. Dual के Pl. कानि.

Now we take up the declension of इदम्. Its Nom. forms are इदम्, इमे, इमानि ॥

Vārtika:—In the Neuter, where there is Anvādeśa or re-employment it should be stated that एनद् replaces इदम्.

Thus एनत्, एने, एनानि ; Ins. S. एनेन Gen. D. एनयोः &c.

Now, we take up the declension of ब्रह्मन्. It is declined as:

Nom. Sing. ब्रह्म Dual. ब्रह्मणी Pl. ब्रह्माणि Voc. हे ब्रह्मन् or हे ब्रह्म.

Now we take up the declension of अहन्. By VIII. 2. 69. S. 172, र् is substituted for the final न् of अहन् and thus अहर्भाति in the Nominative Sg. Had there been रुँ, then the र् would have been changed to उ by हशि च VI. 1. 114 S. 166. The form would have been अहोभाति in the Nom. Sing.

In the N. D. by VI. 4. 136. S. 237, the अ of अन् portion of अहन् is optionally elided and thus we get अह्नी or अहनी. N. Pl. is अहानि ॥

Before भ्याम् &c, where अहन् gets the designation of pada, the following rule applies.
